section.title: Okuma evi 1
section.description: Yoğun okuma: fen, sağlık ve sosyal konularda 48 özgün metin, her ünitede bir okuma stratejisi ve cümle çözümleme; sonunda 40 soruluk tanı denemesi

units.title: Önce soruyu oku
units.description: Kısa metinler: önce soruyu oku, sonra ara
units.guide:
## Strateji
YDS'de okuma parçasını baştan sona ayrıntılı okumak zaman kaybıdır. **Önce soruyu oku**: soru kökü sana neyi araman gerektiğini söyler. Ana fikir sorusu metnin geneline, ayrıntı sorusu tek bir cümleye, gönderim sorusu (*they, it*) yakındaki bir isme bakar. Ne aradığını bilen okuyucu daha hızlı okur ve dikkatini doğru yere verir.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Metne geçmeden soru kökünü oku ve türünü belirle: ana fikir mi, ayrıntı mı, gönderim mi, kelime mi?
2. Kökteki anahtar kelimeyi seç (ör. *length of the dance*).
3. Metni hızlıca tara, anahtar kelimeyi ya da eş anlamlısını bul.
4. O cümleyi ve bir önceki cümleyi dikkatle oku.
5. Şıkları metindeki bilgiyle karşılaştır; metinde olmayanı ele.

## Örnek
*Bees gather around the dancer. The length of the dance shows the distance to the food.*
Soru: "According to the passage, the length of the dance shows ----." Anahtar kelime *length*; ikinci cümle cevabı verir: *the distance*. İlk cümleyi ayrıntılı okumana gerek yok.

## Sınav ipucu
Metinde geçen kelimeleri tekrar eden şık her zaman doğru değildir. YDS çeldiricileri metnin kelimelerini kullanıp yanlış bir şey söyler. Şıkkı, metindeki cümlenin **anlamıyla** karşılaştır.

nodes.title: Fen: Arılar ve yanardağlar
nodes.description: Metin 1: Bal arıları yiyeceğin yerini dansla nasıl anlatır? Metin 2: Bilim insanları yanardağları nasıl izler? ys5 kelimeleri: waste, gather, enable, observe, scientist, researcher, device, demonstrate ve 29 kelime daha.

exercises.passage:
Honeybees live in large groups, and they depend on each other to find food. When a worker bee discovers a field of flowers, it returns to the hive and performs a special movement which is known as the waggle dance. This dance was described in detail by Karl von Frisch, an Austrian scientist who later won the Nobel Prize for his work.

The dance carries two important pieces of information. The direction of the dance shows the direction of the food in relation to the sun, and the length of the dance shows the distance. A long dance means that the flowers are far away, while a short one means that they are nearby. Other bees gather around the dancer, follow its movements and then fly out to the same place.

Researchers have used cameras and small electronic devices to observe this behaviour more accurately. Their results demonstrate that bees can communicate complex information without words. This system enables a whole colony to collect food rapidly and to avoid wasted journeys, which is vital for its survival, especially in seasons when flowers are rare.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bees fly long distances because flowers are rare in most seasons.
Cameras and electronic devices are now used to protect honeybee colonies.
Honeybees use a special dance to tell other bees where food can be found.
Bees gather around the hive at night in order to stay warm together.
Karl von Frisch won the Nobel Prize because he kept bees for many years.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…a special dance to tell other bees where food can be found’: metnin her paragrafı bu dansı anlatır. ‘Nobel’ ödülü yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır ve arı beslemekle ilgili değildir; ‘distances’ seçeneği metinde olmayan bir neden kurar; ‘protect’ yanlıştır, cihazlar dansı gözlemlemek için kullanılır; ‘night’ ve ısınma metinde geçmez.

exercises.passage:
Volcanoes can be dangerous, but today scientists are often able to warn people before an eruption, which is the moment when hot rock and gas burst out of a mountain. To do this, volcanoes are watched closely by teams who use many different instruments.

One important signal is the movement of the ground. Before an eruption, hot liquid rock rises beneath the volcano and pushes the surface up slightly. This change is measured by special devices which can detect movements of less than a centimetre. Scientists also count small earthquakes, because their frequency often increases when rock is moving underground. In addition, the gases that come out of the volcano are collected and analysed, since a sudden change in these gases can point to danger.

Satellites help as well. They take pictures from space and show changes in the heat and shape of a mountain. However, no method is perfect, and some eruptions still happen without clear warning. For this reason, experts combine all the data and share it with local governments, which then decide whether people should leave their homes.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: the damage that eruptions cause to nearby towns
the history of satellites and pictures from space
the decisions local governments make after earthquakes
the reasons why volcanoes become active underground
the methods scientists use to warn people before an eruption
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the methods scientists use to warn people…’: metin yer hareketi, küçük depremler, gazlar ve uydular gibi izleme yollarını anlatır. ‘active’ seçeneğindeki nedenler açıklanmaz; ‘damage’ ve kasabalar metinde yoktur; ‘history’ uyduların tarihi anlatılmaz; ‘decisions’ yalnızca son cümlede geçen bir ayrıntıdır.

nodes.title: Sağlık: Uyku ve yürüyüş
nodes.description: Metin 1: Gençlerde uyku ve hafıza. Metin 2: Her gün yürümenin sağlığa yararları. ys5 kelimeleri: gather, teenager, experiment, scientist, brain, anxiety, harm, mood ve 17 kelime daha.

exercises.passage:
Many teenagers go to bed late and wake up early for school, so they often get less sleep than they need. Doctors recommend that people between the ages of thirteen and eighteen sleep for about eight to ten hours a night, but surveys suggest that a large proportion of them sleep much less.

Sleep is not only a time of rest for the body. During sleep, the brain is busy with an important task: it sorts the information which was gathered during the day and stores the most useful parts. In several experiments, students who slept well after learning new words remembered them better than students who stayed awake. Scientists believe that new memories are strengthened mainly during deep sleep.

A lack of sleep can therefore harm learning, but its effects go further. Tired teenagers are more likely to have problems with mood and concentration, and some studies link short sleep to anxiety. For this reason, some schools in the United States and elsewhere have been encouraged to start classes later in the morning. Early results from these schools suggest that students who sleep longer arrive on time more often and pay more attention in class.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Schools in the United States have stopped giving homework to tired students.
Deep sleep is more important for adults than for teenagers.
Most teenagers sleep for more than ten hours a night.
Many teenagers do not get enough sleep, and this can harm memory and learning.
Teenagers should study new words late at night before they go to bed.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Many teenagers do not get enough sleep…’: metin az uykuyu ve bunun öğrenmeye etkisini anlatır. ‘night’ ile geç saatte çalışma önerisi metinde yoktur; ‘homework’ söz konusu edilmez, okullar derse geç başlar; ‘adults’ ile karşılaştırma yapılmaz; ‘hours’ seçeneği ters bilgidir, gençlerin çoğu daha az uyur.

exercises.passage:
Walking is one of the simplest forms of physical activity, and it costs nothing. Doctors often advise adults to walk for at least thirty minutes a day, and research which has followed large groups of people for many years supports this advice.

Regular walking strengthens the heart and helps to control blood pressure. It also burns calories, so it can play a part in the fight against obesity, which is a growing problem in many countries. In addition, walking is good for bones and muscles, especially in elderly people, who are more likely to fall and break a bone. Studies have shown that people who walk every day have a lower risk of diabetes and some types of cancer.

The benefits are not only physical. Walking, especially in green places such as parks, is often linked to better mood and lower stress. Many people say that a short walk helps them to think more clearly. Experts point out that the walk does not have to be fast or long to be useful. Even ten minutes after each meal can make a difference, and the habit is easily kept up because no special equipment is needed.
exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: describe the history of parks in big cities
warn elderly people about the dangers of falling
advertise special equipment for fast walkers
explain the health benefits of walking every day
compare walking with running and swimming
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain the health benefits of walking every day’: üç paragraf da yürüyüşün bedene ve ruha yararını anlatır. ‘compare’ yanlıştır, koşu ve yüzme geçmez; ‘history’ parkların tarihi anlatılmaz; ‘falling’ yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır; ‘advertise’ ters bilgidir, özel ekipman gerekmez.

nodes.title: Sosyal: Bahçeler ve kütüphaneler
nodes.description: Metin 1: Şehirlerdeki topluluk bahçeleri. Metin 2: Halk kütüphaneleri nasıl değişiyor? ys5 kelimeleri: spread, attract, cultural, urban, exchange, seed, heat, rapidly ve 11 kelime daha.

exercises.passage:
In many large cities, people who live in flats have no garden of their own. Community gardens offer a solution. These are pieces of public or empty land which are shared by local people, who grow vegetables, fruit and flowers together.

Such gardens have spread rapidly over the past few decades. In New York, for example, hundreds of gardens were created on empty land in the 1970s, when many buildings in poor neighbourhoods had been left unused. Today, similar projects can be found in cities from Berlin to Istanbul.

Community gardens bring several benefits. First, they provide fresh, cheap food, which is especially valuable for families on low incomes. Second, they improve the urban environment: plants clean the air, reduce heat in summer and attract birds and insects. Perhaps most importantly, the gardens bring neighbours together. People of different ages and cultural backgrounds work side by side, exchange seeds and advice, and get to know each other. exercises.passage:
For centuries, public libraries were places where people went mainly to borrow books. Currently their role is changing quickly, and many libraries are being transformed into modern community centres.

One reason for this change is technology. Much information is now available online, so fewer people visit libraries only to find facts. In response, libraries have added computers, free internet access and digital services, such as electronic books which can be borrowed from home. Some libraries even lend unusual items like musical instruments, tools or cameras.

Libraries are also used for a wide range of activities. Children attend reading clubs, adults take language or computer courses, and people who are looking for work get help with writing a CV. In many cities, the library is one of the few indoor public places where people can stay for hours without paying anything. This is especially important for elderly people, students and families on low incomes, who may have no quiet place to study at home.

Not everything is positive, however. In several countries, library budgets have been reduced, and some branches have closed. Supporters argue that libraries are vital for an equal society, because they give everyone access to knowledge.

nodes.title: Cümle çözümleme
nodes.description: Ünitedeki metinlerden uzun cümleler: ana fiil, which/who bağlantısı ve Türkçe karşılık (özne + ana fiil + nesne iskeleti)

exercises.question: ‘In several experiments, students who slept well after learning new words remembered them better than students who stayed awake.’ Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir?
options: learning
stayed
experiments
slept
remembered
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘remembered’. İskelet: students (özne) + remembered (ana fiil) + them (nesne). ‘slept’ ve ‘stayed’ who ile başlayan yan cümlelerin fiilleridir; ‘learning’ after edatından sonra gelen -ing biçimidir; ‘experiments’ bir isimdir.

exercises.question: ‘This change is measured by special devices which can detect movements of less than a centimetre.’ Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir?
options: devices
is measured
movements
can detect
change
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘is measured’ (edilgen). İskelet: This change (özne) + is measured (ana fiil) + by special devices. ‘can detect’ which yan cümlesinin fiilidir; ‘change’ öznenin kendisidir; ‘devices’ ve ‘movements’ isimdir.

exercises.question: ‘Shopkeepers who sold the same goods worked together in associations, which set prices and protected the quality of the products.’ Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir?
options: goods
sold
set
protected
worked
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘worked’. İskelet: Shopkeepers (özne) + worked (ana fiil) + together in associations. ‘sold’ who yan cümlesindedir; ‘set’ ve ‘protected’ which yan cümlesinin fiilleridir; ‘goods’ isimdir.

exercises.question: ‘First, they provide fresh, cheap food, which is especially valuable for families on low incomes.’ Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir?
options: fresh, cheap food
families
low incomes
the gardens
the city
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘fresh, cheap food’: virgülden hemen önceki isim öbeğidir; değerli olan yiyecektir. ‘families’ ve ‘low incomes’ which'ten sonra gelir, onu nitelemez; ‘the gardens’ they ile anılır; ‘the city’ cümlede geçmez.

exercises.question: ‘Experts combine all the data and share it with local governments, which then decide whether people should leave their homes.’ Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir?
options: experts
people
their homes
local governments
all the data
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘local governments’: karar veren yerel yönetimlerdir; which hemen önceki isme bağlanır. ‘all the data’ karar veremez; ‘experts’ cümlenin öznesidir, yan cümleye bağlanmaz; ‘people’ ve ‘their homes’ which'ten sonra gelir.

exercises.question: ‘Much information is now available online, so fewer people visit libraries only to find facts.’ Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?
options: Artık pek çok bilgi internette bulunduğu için kimse kütüphaneleri ziyaret etmiyor.
Artık çok az bilgi internette bulunduğu için daha çok kişi kütüphanelerde bilgi arıyor.
Artık pek çok bilgi internette bulunduğu için daha az kişi kütüphaneleri yalnızca bilgi bulmak için ziyaret ediyor.
Artık pek çok bilgi internette bulunduğu için daha fazla kişi kütüphaneleri yalnızca bilgi bulmak için ziyaret ediyor.
Eskiden pek çok bilgi internette bulunduğu için daha az kişi kütüphaneleri yalnızca bilgi bulmak için ziyaret ediyordu.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…daha az kişi… ziyaret ediyor’: iki yan cümle so ile bağlanmış; fewer people = daha az kişi, now = artık. ‘fazla’ fewer'ı ters çevirir; ‘eskiden’ zamanı geçmişe taşır; ‘kimse’ olumsuzluğu abartır; ‘arıyor’ seçeneği bilginin az olduğunu söyler.

exercises.question: ‘Many gardens face a serious problem, because the land is often owned by the city or by private companies.’ Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?
options: Pek çok bahçe ciddi bir sorunla karşı karşıya kalacak, çünkü belediye araziyi şirketlere verecek.
Pek çok bahçe ciddi bir sorunla karşı karşıyadır, çünkü arazi hiçbir zaman belediyeye ya da özel şirketlere ait değildir.
Pek çok bahçe ciddi bir sorunla karşı karşıyadır, çünkü arazi çoğu zaman belediyeye ya da özel şirketlere aittir.
Pek çok bahçe ciddi bir sorun yaratır, çünkü şirketler araziyi belediyeden satın alır.
Birkaç bahçe küçük bir sorunla karşılaştı, çünkü arazi özel şirketlere satıldı.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…arazi çoğu zaman belediyeye ya da özel şirketlere aittir’: is owned (edilgen) = aittir/sahiplidir, often = çoğu zaman. ‘hiçbir’ olumsuz yapar; ‘yaratır’ bahçeyi sorunun kaynağı yapar; ‘birkaç’ ve ‘satıldı’ özneyi ve zamanı değiştirir; ‘kalacak’ geleceğe taşır.

exercises.question: ‘The dance was described in detail by Karl von Frisch, an Austrian scientist who later won the Nobel Prize.’ Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?
options: Dans, daha sonra Nobel Ödülü'nü kazanan Avusturyalı bilim insanı Karl von Frisch tarafından ayrıntılı olarak tanımlandı.
Daha sonra Nobel Ödülü'nü kazanan Avusturyalı bilim insanı Karl von Frisch, dansı ilk kez gördü.
Dans, Nobel Ödülü'nü daha önce kazanmış olan Avusturyalı bir bilim insanını etkiledi.
Dans, Avusturyalı bilim insanı Karl von Frisch tarafından ayrıntılı olarak tanımlanmadı.
Avusturyalı bilim insanı Karl von Frisch, dansı tanımladığı için hiçbir ödül kazanmadı.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…tarafından ayrıntılı olarak tanımlandı’: was described by = … tarafından tanımlandı; who later won = daha sonra kazanan. ‘gördü’ fiili değiştirir; ‘etkiledi’ ve ‘önce’ hem fiili hem zamanı bozar; ‘tanımlanmadı’ olumsuzdur; ‘kazanmadı’ ödülü inkâr eder.

exercises.question: ‘Even ten minutes after each meal can make a difference.’ Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?
options: Her yemekten sonra on dakika hiçbir fark yaratmaz.
Yemeklerden sonra on dakikadan fazlası fark yaratır.
Her yemekten sonra on dakika fark yaratmıştı.
Her yemekten sonra on dakika bile fark yaratabilir.
Her yemekten önce en az on dakika yürümek gerekir.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Her yemekten sonra on dakika bile fark yaratabilir.’: even = bile, can = -ebilir. ‘gerekir’ zorunluluk ekler ve after yerine önce der; ‘yaratmaz’ olumsuzdur; ‘fazlası’ even anlamını kaybeder; ‘yaratmıştı’ zamanı geçmişe taşır.

exercises.passage:
The Grand Bazaar in Istanbul is one of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world. Its history began soon after 1453, when Sultan Mehmed II ordered the construction of a stone building for the trade of valuable goods such as cloth and jewellery. Over the following centuries, more buildings and streets were added around this centre, until the market became an enormous city of its own.

Today the Grand Bazaar has more than sixty streets and about four thousand shops, which sell carpets, gold, leather, lamps and many other products. In the past, each street was occupied by a single trade, and some street names still remind visitors of this tradition. Shopkeepers who sold the same goods worked together in associations, which set prices and protected the quality of the products.

Thanks to careful repairs, the market has survived several disasters. It was badly damaged by fires and by a strong earthquake in 1894, but each time it was repaired and opened again. Now it attracts millions of tourists every year, although many local people continue to shop there as well. For many visitors, discussing the price with the shopkeeper is part of the experience.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Tourists have replaced local people as the only customers of the market.

Sultan Mehmed II designed every street of the market himself.
The Grand Bazaar was built after a strong earthquake destroyed the old market.
Shopkeepers in the Grand Bazaar decide prices without any rules.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…has grown over centuries and is still an important market today’: metin çarşının büyümesini ve bugünkü önemini anlatır. ‘destroyed’ yanlıştır, çarşı depremden sonra onarılmıştır; ‘rules’ ters bilgidir, dernekler fiyat belirler; ‘replaced’ yanlıştır, yerel halk da alışveriş yapar; ‘designed’ metinde yoktur, Sultan yalnızca ilk binayı yaptırmıştır.

exercises.passage:
Every year, people throw away millions of old phones, computers and televisions. This electronic waste, or e-waste, is one of the fastest-growing types of rubbish in the world. According to the United Nations, more than fifty million tonnes are produced each year, but less than a quarter is collected and recycled properly.

E-waste is a serious problem because many devices contain dangerous substances such as lead and mercury, which can harm human health. When old electronics are thrown away with ordinary rubbish, these chemicals may enter the soil and water. In some poorer countries, large amounts of e-waste are handled by workers who burn the plastic parts to get the valuable metals inside. The smoke from this burning damages their health.

At the same time, e-waste is also a resource. Phones and computers contain small amounts of gold, silver and copper, which can be recovered and used again. Experts say that the best solution is to repair devices and use them for longer. Some governments now require companies to make products that are easier to fix, and several cities have set up special points where people can leave their old electronics.

options: the dangers of electronic waste and possible ways to reduce it
the history of the United Nations
why new phones are better than old ones

the high price of gold, silver and copper
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the dangers of electronic waste and possible ways to reduce it’: metin e-atığın zararlarını ve çözümlerini anlatır. ‘produced’ yanlıştır, üretim değil atık konu edilir; ‘price’ metalların fiyatından söz edilmez; ‘history’ BM yalnızca kaynak olarak anılır; ‘better’ yeni telefonlar övülmez.

Every year, people throw away millions of old phones, computers and televisions. This electronic waste, or e-waste, is one of the fastest-growing types of rubbish in the world. According to the United Nations, more than fifty million tonnes are produced each year, but less than a quarter is collected and recycled properly.

E-waste is a serious problem because many devices contain dangerous substances such as lead and mercury, which can harm human health. When old electronics are thrown away with ordinary rubbish, these chemicals may enter the soil and water. In some poorer countries, large amounts of e-waste are handled by workers who burn the plastic parts to get the valuable metals inside. The smoke from this burning damages their health.

At the same time, e-waste is also a resource. Phones and computers contain small amounts of gold, silver and copper, which can be recovered and used again. Experts say that the best solution is to repair devices and use them for longer. Some governments now require companies to make products that are easier to fix, and several cities have set up special points where people can leave their old electronics.
exercises.question: According to the passage, workers in some poorer countries ----.
options: turn old computers into new products
repair old phones and sell them again
collect e-waste for the United Nations
burn plastic parts to get the metals inside devices
are paid to produce new televisions
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘burn plastic parts to get the metals inside devices’: metinde açıkça yazar. ‘sell’ seçeneğindeki onarım işçilerle ilgili değildir, uzmanların önerisidir; ‘Nations’ için toplama yapıldığı söylenmez; ‘paid’ ve televizyon üretimi metinde yoktur; ‘turn’ seçeneği metinde geçmeyen bir iş anlatır.

units.title: Ana fikir nerede?
units.description: Konu cümlesini bul: başta mı, sonda mı?
units.guide:
## Strateji
YDS'nin en sık sorduğu soru ana fikirdir: "What is the main idea of the passage?" İngilizce bilgi metinlerinde yazar ana fikri çoğu zaman **ilk paragrafın sonunda** ya da **her paragrafın ilk cümlesinde** (konu cümlesi) verir. Son paragraf ise genellikle sonucu ya da bir sorunu ekler. Nereye bakacağını bilirsen bütün ayrıntıları okumadan ana fikri bulursun.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. İlk paragrafı dikkatle oku; özellikle son cümlesine bak.
2. Diğer paragrafların yalnızca ilk cümlelerini oku.
3. Son paragraftaki *however, as a result* gibi bağlaçları işaretle.
4. Ana fikri kendi Türkçe cümlenle söyle.
5. Şıklardan senin cümlene en yakın, en **genel** olanı seç.

## Örnek
*Tardigrades are tiny animals which can survive extreme conditions. They can live for years without water. Some even survived a trip into space.*
İlk cümle konu cümlesidir: aşırı koşullarda hayatta kalan küçük hayvanlar. Diğer iki cümle bunu destekleyen örneklerdir; "uzay yolculuğu" ana fikir değil, ayrıntıdır.

## Sınav ipucu
Ana fikir sorusunda iki tuzak vardır: metindeki **tek bir ayrıntıyı** (bir sayı, bir isim) anlatan şık ve metni **aşırı genelleyen** şık (*all, always, never*). Doğru şık metnin tamamını kapsar ama metnin söylemediği bir şey eklemez.

exercises.passage:
Tardigrades are tiny animals, usually less than one millimetre long, which live almost everywhere on Earth, from mountain tops to the deep ocean. Because of their round bodies and slow movements, they are sometimes called 'water bears'. They were first described by a German scientist in 1773, but their most remarkable abilities were discovered much later.

When their environment becomes dry, tardigrades lose almost all the water in their bodies and enter a state which looks very similar to death. In this state, their activity stops almost completely, and they can survive for years without food or water. When water returns, they slowly come back to life.

Laboratory experiments have shown that tardigrades in this dry state can resist extreme conditions. They have survived temperatures close to minus 270 degrees, very high pressure and strong radiation. In 2007, some tardigrades were even sent into space, where they were exposed to the conditions outside a spacecraft, and some of them survived the journey. Scientists who study these animals hope to understand how they protect their cells. This knowledge could one day help researchers to store vaccines and other medicines without keeping them cold.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Tardigrades must stay in water all their lives to remain healthy.
Tardigrades are the only animals that live in the deep ocean.
Tardigrades are tiny animals that can survive very difficult conditions.
Vaccines can already be stored for years thanks to tardigrades.
Tardigrades were discovered by a German scientist who travelled into space.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Tardigrades are tiny animals that can survive very difficult conditions.’: ilk paragraftaki "remarkable abilities" ifadesi metnin konusunu verir, diğer paragraflar bunu destekler. ‘travelled’ yanlıştır, uzaya bilim insanı değil hayvanlar gönderilmiştir; ‘healthy’ ters bilgidir, susuz yıllarca yaşarlar; ‘only’ aşırı genellemedir; ‘already’ yanlıştır, bu yalnızca gelecekteki bir umuttur.

exercises.passage:
In autumn, the leaves of many trees turn yellow, orange and red before they fall. This change of colour is caused by chemical processes inside the leaf, which depend on light and temperature.

During spring and summer, leaves are green because they contain large amounts of chlorophyll, a substance which plants use to capture energy from sunlight. Chlorophyll is constantly broken down and replaced while the days are long and warm. Leaves also contain yellow and orange substances, but in summer these colours are hidden by the strong green.

When the days become shorter and colder, the tree stops producing new chlorophyll. As the green slowly disappears, the yellow and orange colours, which were present all along, become visible. Red colours have a different origin. They are produced only in autumn by some trees, such as maples, especially when the days are sunny and the nights are cool. Scientists think that these red substances may protect the leaf from too much light while the tree moves useful nutrients from the leaves into its branches and roots. Afterwards, the leaves are no longer needed, and the tree lets them fall to save water during winter.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Maple trees are the only trees whose leaves change colour.
Leaves turn red because of cold rain in autumn.
Chlorophyll protects trees from too much light in winter.
Trees lose their leaves because red substances damage them.
Autumn colours appear because trees stop making the green substance in their leaves.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…trees stop making the green substance in their leaves’: yeşil madde azalınca diğer renkler görünür; metnin çekirdeği budur. ‘damage’ yanlıştır, kırmızı maddeler yaprağı korur; ‘only’ aşırı genellemedir; ‘rain’ metinde geçmez; ‘winter’ yanlıştır, kışın klorofil üretilmez.

exercises.passage:
Soft drinks such as cola are popular all over the world, but they often contain a surprising amount of sugar. A typical can of cola contains about 35 grams of sugar, which is roughly seven small spoons. The World Health Organization advises adults to keep added sugar below about 50 grams a day, so one can provides most of the daily maximum.

The main problem is that sugar in drinks is consumed quickly and does not make people feel full. As a result, people who drink soft drinks regularly often take in extra calories without eating less food. Over time, this habit has been linked to weight gain, obesity and type 2 diabetes, a disease in which the body cannot control blood sugar properly. Sugary drinks also damage teeth, because the bacteria in the mouth produce acids from sugar.

In response, a number of countries, including the United Kingdom and Mexico, have introduced special taxes on sugary drinks. Many companies then reduced the amount of sugar in their products in order to avoid the tax. Health experts welcome such measures, but they also argue that water remains the best choice for everyday thirst.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Mexico was the first country to ban soft drinks.
Sugar in food is more harmful than sugar in drinks.
Companies have stopped adding sugar to all their drinks.

exercises.passage:
Soft drinks such as cola are popular all over the world, but they often contain a surprising amount of sugar. A typical can of cola contains about 35 grams of sugar, which is roughly seven small spoons. The World Health Organization advises adults to keep added sugar below about 50 grams a day, so one can provides most of the daily maximum.

The main problem is that sugar in drinks is consumed quickly and does not make people feel full. As a result, people who drink soft drinks regularly often take in extra calories without eating less food. Over time, this habit has been linked to weight gain, obesity and type 2 diabetes, a disease in which the body cannot control blood sugar properly. Sugary drinks also damage teeth, because the bacteria in the mouth produce acids from sugar.

In response, a number of countries, including the United Kingdom and Mexico, have introduced special taxes on sugary drinks. Many companies then reduced the amount of sugar in their products in order to avoid the tax. Health experts welcome such measures, but they also argue that water remains the best choice for everyday thirst.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘contains most of the sugar an adult should have in a day’: "one can provides most of the daily maximum". ‘fifty’ günlük sınırdır, kutudaki miktar 35 gramdır; ‘enough’ ve diyabet tek kutuyla ilişkilendirilmez; ‘full’ ters bilgidir, tok tutmaz; ‘extra’ kalori alındığı söylenir.

exercises.passage:
Today, washing hands is known as one of the simplest ways to prevent disease, but this idea was not always accepted. In the 1840s, Ignaz Semmelweis, a Hungarian doctor who worked in a large hospital in Vienna, noticed a strange difference between two of its clinics.

In the first clinic, where mothers were cared for by doctors and medical students, many women died of a fever soon after giving birth. In the second clinic, which was run by specially trained women, far fewer mothers died. Semmelweis observed that the doctors often came directly from examining dead bodies. He concluded that they were carrying something harmful on their hands, even though bacteria had not yet been discovered.

In 1847 he ordered all doctors to wash their hands in a chemical solution before examining patients. As a result, the number of deaths in his clinic fell sharply. However, many senior doctors rejected his ideas, partly because they did not want to accept that they themselves were causing deaths. Semmelweis died in 1865, and his work was appreciated only years later, when scientists such as Louis Pasteur proved that tiny living things cause infection.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a doctor whose idea about hand washing was accepted only after his death’: ilk cümle "this idea was not always accepted" der, son cümle geç gelen kabulü anlatır. ‘history’ hastanelerin tarihi anlatılmaz; ‘Pasteur’ yalnızca son cümlede geçer; ‘microscope’ metinde yoktur; ‘preferred’ kadınların tercihi söylenmez.

nodes.description: Metin 1: Dört günlük çalışma haftası denemeleri. Metin 2: İki dille büyüyen çocuklar. ys5 kelimeleri: wage, trial, researcher, stress, extra, suitable, instead of, as a consequence ve 10 kelime daha.

exercises.passage:
In recent years, a number of companies in countries such as the United Kingdom, Iceland and Spain have tested a four-day working week. In most of these trials, employees worked about 32 hours a week instead of 40, but their wages stayed the same. The idea is that people who are less tired can do the same amount of work in less time.

One of the largest trials took place in the United Kingdom in 2022, when around 60 companies and nearly 3,000 workers took part. The results were studied by researchers who collected information about sales, sick days and the health of workers. Most companies reported that their results stayed the same or even improved, while employees said they felt less stress and slept better. As a consequence, the majority of the companies decided to continue with the new system after the trial ended.

However, the four-day week is not suitable for every job. In hospitals, schools and shops, which must stay open for fixed hours, more workers would be needed to cover the extra day. Critics also point out that the companies which joined the trials chose to do so, so they may have been especially likely to succeed.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Most companies stopped the four-day week after the trial.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Trials suggest that a four-day week can work, though not for every job.’: ikinci paragraf olumlu sonuçları, son paragraf sınırları verir; ana fikir ikisini birleştirir. ‘earned’ yanlıştır, ücretler aynı kaldı; ‘stopped’ ters bilgidir, çoğu devam etti; ‘successful’ yanlıştır, hastane ve okullar uygun olmayan örneklerdir; ‘five’ seçeneği metnin fikrini tersine çevirir.

exercises.passage:
Around the world, millions of children grow up speaking two languages. Some learn one language from their mother and another from their father, while others speak one language at home and a different one at school. In Germany, for example, many children whose families are of Turkish origin grow up with both Turkish and German.

In the past, some parents and teachers worried that two languages would confuse young children and slow down their development. Research which has been carried out since the 1960s does not support this belief. Bilingual children, that is, children who use two languages, may know fewer words in each language at first, but the total number of words they know is usually similar to that of other children. Moreover, mixing the two languages in one sentence is normal and is not a sign of confusion.

Some studies have also suggested that bilingual children are better at switching their attention between tasks, although this result has been questioned by other researchers. What experts agree on is that children need regular, rich contact with both languages. If one language is used only rarely, it may slowly be forgotten.

options: Mixing two languages in a sentence is a sign of confusion.
Bilingual children always know more words than other children.
Research shows that growing up with two languages does not harm children.
Turkish children in Germany usually forget Turkish.
Children should learn a second language only after they start school.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…growing up with two languages does not harm children’: ikinci paragrafın konu cümlesi eski korkunun araştırmayla desteklenmediğini söyler. ‘school’ seçeneği metinde önerilmez; ‘sign’ ters bilgidir, karıştırmak normaldir; ‘always’ aşırı genellemedir; ‘forget’ metinde yoktur.

exercises.passage:
Tea is the most popular drink in Turkey, and most of it is grown in the province of Rize on the Black Sea coast. Yet tea growing in the region has a fairly short history. Previously, Turkey bought almost all of its tea from abroad, and coffee was the more common drink.

In the 1920s, the new government looked for crops which could grow in the wet climate of the eastern Black Sea, where farmers were poor and land was limited. Experiments with tea plants were started, and an expert called Zihni Derin, who is often described as the father of Turkish tea, played a leading role. Seeds were brought from Georgia, and the first tea gardens were set up on the steep slopes near the sea. The first tea factory in Rize was opened in 1947.

Tea growing rapidly transformed the economy of the region. Today, hundreds of thousands of families earn part of their income from tea, and Turkey's annual production places it among the largest tea producers in the world. However, the industry also faces problems. Most tea is still picked by hand, labour is hard to find, and rising costs have put pressure on small farmers.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Tea is grown in Rize because the land there is flat and dry.
Tea growing in Rize is fairly new, but it has changed the region's economy.
Most tea in Turkey is now picked by machines.
Turkey has always produced its own tea and coffee.
Zihni Derin built the first tea factory in Georgia.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Tea growing in Rize is fairly new, but it has changed the region's economy.’: ilk paragraf "fairly short history" der, son paragraf ekonomideki dönüşümü anlatır. ‘always’ ters bilgidir, çay eskiden dışarıdan alınırdı; ‘built’ ve Gürcistan yanlıştır, Gürcistan tohumların geldiği yerdir; ‘flat’ yanlıştır, iklim yağışlı ve yamaçlar diktir; ‘machines’ ters bilgidir, çay elle toplanır.

exercises.passage:
In the last few years, electric scooters have appeared in many city centres around the world, including Istanbul, Paris and Madrid. Most of them are offered by private companies through rental schemes. Users find a scooter with a mobile app, ride it to their destination and leave it on the street, where the next user can pick it up.

Supporters say that scooters are a cheap and flexible way to travel short distances. They do not produce emissions while they are being used, and they may reduce car traffic if people choose them instead of driving. For many young people, who often do not own a car, they are an attractive alternative to buses.

Critics, however, point to several problems. Scooters which are left on pavements can block the way for elderly and disabled people. Accidents are also common, partly because many riders do not wear helmets, and head injuries are frequently reported by hospitals. In addition, studies suggest that scooter trips often replace walking rather than car journeys, so the environmental benefit may be smaller than expected. As a result, Paris banned rental scooters in 2023 after a public vote, while other cities have introduced speed limits and special parking areas.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Electric scooters offer some benefits, but they also cause several problems.
Scooter riders must wear helmets in every city.
Young people prefer buses to electric scooters.
Electric scooters are the cleanest way to travel in Paris.
Most cities have banned electric scooters since 2023.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…offer some benefits, but they also cause several problems.’: ikinci paragraf yararları, üçüncüsü sorunları anlatır; ana fikir ikisini kapsar. ‘cleanest’ metinde yoktur; ‘Most’ aşırı genellemedir, yasaklayan Paris'tir; ‘must’ yanlıştır, birçok sürücü kask takmaz; ‘prefer’ ters bilgidir.

units.title: Gönderim zincirleri
units.guide:
## Strateji
Yazar aynı şeyi iki kez adıyla söylemez; ikinci kez *it, this, they, them, which, such* gibi gönderim sözcükleriyle anar. Bu sözcükler bir zincir kurar: *a coral → it → this process → it*. Zinciri takip edersen cümleler birbirine bağlanır, metin daha az kopuk görünür ve "The word ‘they’ refers to ----" soruları kolaylaşır.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Gönderim sözcüğünü görünce dur ve bir önceki cümleye dön.
2. Tekil mi çoğul mu bak: *it, this* tekil; *they, them, these* çoğul.
3. Aynı türden en yakın ismi ara: insan mı, nesne mi, olay mı?
4. Bulduğun ismi sözcüğün yerine koyup cümleyi yeniden oku; anlam bozulmuyorsa doğrudur.
5. *this* ve *such* bazen tek bir ismi değil, önceki cümlenin tamamını gösterir.

## Örnek
*Corals live with tiny algae. They give the corals food. When the water gets too warm, this partnership breaks down.*
- **They** → çoğul ve yiyecek veren taraf → *algae* (mercanlar yiyeceği alan taraftır).
- **this partnership** → önceki iki cümlede anlatılan mercan–alg ortaklığı.

## Sınav ipucu
Şıklarda genellikle aynı cümlede geçen birkaç isim olur. Önce tekil/çoğul uyumuna bak; bu çoğu zaman iki üç şıkkı hemen eler. Kalanları cümleye yerleştirip anlamı kontrol et.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Corals are plants which produce food from sunlight with the help of tiny animals.
Warm water can make corals lose their algae, and this threatens reefs around the world.
Bleached corals always die within a few weeks because they cannot find any food.
Breeding new corals has already solved the problem of bleaching on most reefs.
The Great Barrier Reef is the only reef that has been damaged by heat waves.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Warm water can make corals lose their algae…’: metin ısınan suyun ağartmaya yol açtığını ve resiflerin tehlikede olduğunu anlatıyor. ‘plants’ yanlış, mercan bir hayvandır. ‘always’ yanlış, su çabuk soğursa mercan iyileşebilir. ‘solved’ yanlış, uzmanlar bu yöntemlerin yalnızca zaman kazandırdığını söylüyor. ‘only’ metinde desteklenmez.
exercises.passage:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, but they are home to about a quarter of all sea creatures. A coral may look like a plant or a rock, yet it is actually a group of tiny animals. These animals live together with very small algae, which grow inside them and produce food from sunlight. In return, the coral gives the algae a safe home, and this partnership also gives reefs their bright colours.

However, the partnership breaks down easily. When the water stays too warm for several weeks, the coral is put under stress and pushes the algae out. Without them, it loses both its colour and its main source of food. Only its white skeleton can then be seen, so this process is called bleaching. A bleached coral is not dead yet. If the temperature falls again quickly, the algae may return and the animal can recover. If the heat lasts too long, however, it usually dies.

Scientists who study reefs say that bleaching has become more frequent as global temperatures rise. Large parts of the Great Barrier Reef, which lies off the coast of Australia, were damaged by heat waves in recent years. Researchers are now testing ways to protect these places, such as breeding corals that can survive in warmer water. Still, most experts agree that such methods can only buy time. In the long run, the future of reefs depends on cutting the emissions that warm the planet.

options: why the United States army built its own satellites

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how satellite navigation finds a position…’: metnin büyük kısmı sinyalin süresinden konumun hesaplanmasını anlatıyor. ‘army’ yalnızca bir ayrıntı. ‘history’ uzay yolculuğu konusu metinde yok. ‘weather’ son paragraftaki küçük bir ayrıntı. ‘compete’ yanlış, metin rekabetten söz etmiyor.
exercises.passage:
Every time you check a map on your phone, you are using signals from space. Satellite navigation works with a group of about thirty satellites, which travel around the Earth at a height of roughly twenty thousand kilometres. The best known of these systems is GPS, which was built by the United States and was first used by its army. Today it is used by billions of ordinary people for free.

Each satellite carries an extremely accurate clock and constantly sends out a signal. This signal tells receivers two simple things: where the satellite is and what time the message left it. Your phone, which contains a small receiver, measures how long each signal took to arrive. Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, the phone can calculate its distance from that satellite. It needs signals from at least four satellites to work out its position on the surface of the planet.

The method sounds simple, but it depends on very precise timing. An error of only one millionth of a second would move your position by about three hundred metres. For this reason, the clocks are checked and corrected from the ground every day. Buildings, trees and bad weather can also block or weaken the signals, which is why a phone sometimes shows the wrong street in a crowded city. Similar systems have since been developed by Europe, Russia and China, and many modern devices use several of them at the same time.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bacteria are becoming resistant to antibiotics, partly because these drugs are misused.
Penicillin is still the best medicine for every kind of infection.
Viruses cause more deaths than bacteria in most parts of the world.
Farmers are the only group responsible for antibiotic resistance.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Bacteria are becoming resistant…’: metin direncin nasıl oluştuğunu ve yanlış kullanımın onu hızlandırdığını anlatıyor. ‘Penicillin’ yalnızca giriş bilgisidir. ‘Viruses’ ile ilgili böyle bir karşılaştırma yok. ‘Farmers’ çözümlerden biridir, tek sorumlu değil. ‘cheaply’ yanlış; metin yeni ilaçların yavaş ve pahalı geliştirildiğini söylüyor.
exercises.passage:
Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing. Since penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928, these drugs have saved millions of lives. Infections which were once deadly, such as those in wounds after surgery, became easy to treat. Today, however, doctors warn that this success is under threat.

The problem is called antibiotic resistance: when a drug is used, most of the bacteria die, but a few may survive because of small changes in their genes. These survivors multiply and pass their resistance on, so the next infection is harder to treat. Over time, whole populations of bacteria can become resistant to several medicines. This natural process is speeded up when antibiotics are used too often or in the wrong way. Many people, for example, take them for a cold or the flu, which are caused by viruses rather than bacteria. Others stop taking their pills as soon as they feel better, before the full dose is finished.

The World Health Organization describes resistance as one of the greatest threats to global health. Every year, it is linked to more than a million deaths, and the number may rise sharply in the coming decades. Experts suggest several solutions: doctors should prescribe these medicines only when they are really needed, and patients who receive them should complete the treatment. Farmers are also urged to use fewer antibiotics on healthy animals. Finally, new drugs must be developed, although this process is slow and expensive.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the different ways in which noise can damage people's health’: metin işitme kaybını, uyku ve kalp sağlığına etkileri anlatıyor. ‘prefer’ metinde yok. ‘airports’ yalnızca bir örnek. ‘sleeping’ uykudan söz ediliyor ama konu uyku yöntemleri değil. ‘history’ yanlış; hava kirliliği sadece karşılaştırma için anılıyor.
exercises.passage:
Most people think of noise as a simple annoyance, but research suggests that it can also harm our health. Traffic, aircraft and loud music are part of daily life in modern cities, and many residents are exposed to them for hours every day. According to the World Health Organization, noise from roads is the second most harmful environmental factor in Europe, after air pollution.

The most obvious danger is hearing loss. Sounds above a certain level can damage the tiny hair cells which turn sound waves into signals for the brain. Once these cells are destroyed, they cannot grow back, so the loss is permanent. Young people who listen to loud music through headphones for long periods are especially at risk.

Noise can also affect the body in less visible ways. Even when we are asleep, the brain continues to react to sounds. A passing lorry or a barking dog may not wake us up completely, but it can raise our heart rate and break the deep sleep which the body needs for recovery. Over many years, this repeated stress has been linked to high blood pressure and heart disease. Children who live near busy airports have also been found to perform worse in reading tests.

Some cities have started to deal with the problem. Quieter road surfaces are being laid, speed limits are reduced at night, and more trees are planted along busy streets. Individuals can help themselves too, for example by keeping the bedroom on the quiet side of the house.

exercises.question: According to the passage, hearing loss caused by loud sounds is permanent because ----.
options: the damaged hair cells in the ear cannot grow back

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the damaged hair cells in the ear cannot grow back’: 2. paragraf bu hücreler yok edilince yeniden büyümediğini söylüyor. ‘reacting’ ters, beyin uykuda da tepki vermeyi sürdürür. ‘headphones’ bir risk grubu örneğidir, neden değil. ‘pressure’ kalple ilgili bir etkidir. ‘weaker’ metinde yok.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Most remote workers have returned to their offices in big cities.
Small towns in Italy and Spain give away all their houses for free.
Remote work has stopped people from moving to cities forever.
Companies prefer workers who live in distant villages.
Remote work has brought new residents to some small towns, with both good and bad results.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Remote work has brought new residents…’: metin küçük kasabalara gelen yeni sakinleri ve bunun olumlu/olumsuz sonuçlarını anlatıyor. ‘returned’ yanlış, bazıları hiç dönmedi. ‘free’ abartı; bazı evler bir avroya satıldı. ‘forever’ yanlış, uzmanlar eğilimin yalnızca kısmen süreceğini söylüyor. ‘villages’ yanlış, şirketler karma modeli tercih ediyor.
exercises.passage:
For most of the last century, people moved from the countryside to big cities in search of work. Remote work, which became common during the pandemic in 2020, has started to change this pattern, and its effects have been studied by many researchers. When offices closed, millions of employees discovered that they could do their jobs from almost anywhere with a good internet connection. Some of them decided not to come back.

Small towns that had been losing their young people for decades suddenly saw new arrivals. Houses there were cheaper and larger, and the air was cleaner. In Italy and Spain, empty houses in some villages were even sold for one euro to attract new residents. Several regions also offered payments to remote workers who agreed to settle locally for at least a year.

The effects on these towns have been mixed. On the positive side, new residents spend money in local shops and cafés, and some schools that were about to close have gained pupils. On the other hand, house prices have risen in popular places, which makes life harder for local families with lower wages. Some locals also complain that the newcomers work for distant companies and take little part in community life.

Experts believe that the trend will continue, but only partly. Many companies now prefer a mixed model, in which staff come to the office two or three days a week. This means that workers still need to live within a reasonable distance of a city. Towns which have fast internet and good transport links are therefore likely to benefit most.

options: local schools have been forced to close

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: why elderly people should not live alone
how helping others without pay can also benefit the volunteers
the chemicals that the brain releases during exercise
the problems that retirement causes for most people
why volunteers should work more than two hours a day
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how helping others without pay can also benefit the volunteers’: metin gönüllülüğün gönüllülere sağladığı faydaları anlatıyor. ‘alone’ yalnızca bir gönüllülük örneğinde geçer. ‘exercise’ metinde yok. ‘retirement’ bir ayrıntıdır. ‘day’ yanlış; metin haftada iki saatten söz ediyor.
exercises.passage:
Volunteering means giving your time to help others without being paid for it. People volunteer in many different ways: they serve meals at shelters, clean beaches, teach children to read or visit elderly neighbours who live alone. Although the main aim is to help the community, researchers have found that volunteers themselves gain a great deal from the experience.

Several large studies, which followed thousands of adults for many years, have linked regular volunteering with better mental health. Volunteers report lower levels of depression and higher life satisfaction than people who do not volunteer. Some research even suggests that older volunteers tend to live longer. Of course, it is possible that healthier and happier people are simply more likely to volunteer in the first place. However, studies in which the same people were observed before and after they started volunteering also show an improvement in mood.

Psychologists offer several explanations for these benefits. Helping others gives people a sense of purpose, which is especially valuable after retirement or the loss of a job. Volunteering is also a social activity, so it reduces loneliness, a problem that is increasingly seen as a serious risk to health. Finally, kind acts seem to release chemicals in the brain that make us feel good.

The amount of time matters too. Researchers have noticed that the benefits appear with as little as two hours a week. Doing too much, on the other hand, can lead to stress, especially when volunteering is felt as a duty rather than a choice.

exercises.question: According to the passage, studies that observed the same people before and after they began volunteering ----.
options: found no change in their mental health

were carried out on young children
proved that volunteers always live longer
also found an improvement in mood
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘also found an improvement in mood’: 2. paragrafın son cümlesi bunu açıkça söylüyor. ‘change’ ters, ruh hâlinde iyileşme bulundu. ‘healthy’ yalnızca bir olasılık olarak anılıyor. ‘children’ metinde yok, çalışmalar yetişkinlerle yapıldı. ‘proved’ abartı; metin “some research suggests” diyor.

nodes.description: Ünitenin metinlerinden uzun cümleler: ana fiil, which ve çeviri

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Small towns that had been losing their young people for decades suddenly saw new arrivals.’
options: had been losing
towns
arrivals
saw
decades
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘saw’. İskelet: Small towns (özne) + saw (ana fiil) + new arrivals (nesne). ‘had been losing’ that ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘towns’ öznedir, ‘arrivals’ nesnedir, ‘decades’ ise süre bildiren bir isimdir.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘Large parts of the Great Barrier Reef, which lies off the coast of Australia, were damaged by heat waves in recent years.’
options: Large parts
the Great Barrier Reef
the coast
Australia
heat waves
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the Great Barrier Reef’: ‘which’ hemen önündeki isme bağlanır ve fiil tekil (lies). ‘Large parts’ çoğul, ‘lies’ ile uyuşmaz ve cümlenin öznesidir (ana fiil: were damaged). ‘the coast’ yan cümlenin içindedir. ‘Australia’ kıyının yeridir. ‘heat waves’ ana cümlenin sonundadır.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Your phone, which contains a small receiver, measures how long each signal took to arrive.’
options: contains
took
arrive
receiver
measures
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘measures’. İskelet: Your phone (özne) + measures (ana fiil) + how long… (nesne cümlesi). ‘contains’ which ile başlayan ara cümlenin fiilidir. ‘took’ nesne cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘arrive’ mastardır. ‘receiver’ bir isimdir.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘Many people, for example, take them for a cold or the flu, which are caused by viruses rather than bacteria.’
options: Many people
viruses

bacteria
them
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a cold or the flu’: virüslerin neden olduğu şey soğuk algınlığı ve griptir; ‘which’ hemen önündeki bu iki hastalığa bağlanır. ‘Many people’ virüslerden kaynaklanmaz. ‘viruses’ ve ‘bacteria’ yan cümlenin içindedir. ‘them’ antibiyotikleri gösterir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Several large studies, which followed thousands of adults for many years, have linked regular volunteering with better mental health.’
options: have linked
followed
volunteering
adults
regular
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘have linked’. İskelet: Several large studies (özne) + have linked (ana fiil) + regular volunteering (nesne). ‘followed’ which ara cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘volunteering’ burada isim (nesne) olarak kullanılıyor. ‘adults’ yan cümledeki nesnedir. ‘regular’ bir sıfattır.

options: Bu hücreler yok edilmeden önce yeniden büyüyebilir, bu yüzden kayıp geçicidir.
Bu hücreler yok edildiğinde yavaşça yeniden büyürler, bu yüzden kayıp kısa sürer.
Bu hücreleri yok eden ses kalıcı bir kayba yol açmaz.
Bu hücreler bir kez yok edildiğinde yeniden büyüyemezler, bu yüzden kayıp kalıcıdır.
Beyin bu hücreleri yok ettiğinde kayıp kalıcı olur.

İskelet: they (özne) + cannot grow back (olumsuz fiil); once = -dığında. ‘geçicidir’ permanent sözcüğünün tersidir. ‘yavaşça’ olumsuzluğu kaldırıyor. ‘açmaz’ cümleyi olumsuz yapıyor. ‘Beyin’ cümlede olmayan bir özne ekliyor.

İskelet: This natural process (özne) + is speeded up (edilgen fiil) + when… (zaman yan cümlesi). ‘yavaşlar’ fiili tersine çeviriyor. ‘hiç’ koşulu değiştiriyor. ‘durdu’ hem anlamı hem zamanı bozuyor. ‘doktorlar’ cümlede olmayan bir özne.

Araştırmacılar bu yerleri korumanın hiçbir yolunun olmadığını düşünüyor.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The Silk Road was a long-lasting network that carried goods, ideas and even diseases between East and West.
The Silk Road was a single road that merchants travelled from China to Europe.
Silk was the only product that was traded between China and the Mediterranean.

Sea routes were dangerous, so trade stayed on land until modern times.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The Silk Road was a long-lasting network…’: metin yolların mal, fikir ve hastalık taşıdığını anlatıyor. ‘single’ ters, metin “not a single road” diyor. ‘only’ yanlış, baharat, kâğıt, cam gibi başka mallar da taşındı. ‘Caravanserais’ şehir değil, hanlardı. ‘dangerous’ ters, deniz yolları daha güvenli hâle geldi.
exercises.passage:
The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes which connected China with the Mediterranean world. It was used for more than fifteen hundred years, from about the second century BC until the fifteenth century. The name itself is quite modern: it was introduced by a German geographer in the nineteenth century, long after the routes had lost their importance.

Silk was the most famous product which moved west, and for centuries the Chinese kept the method of making it a secret. However, many other goods were also carried along the routes, including spices, paper, glass, horses and precious metals. Few merchants travelled the whole distance. Instead, goods passed from one trader to another, and prices rose at each stage. Cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara, where caravans stopped to rest and trade, grew rich as a result. Anatolia was also an important link, and many large inns called caravanserais were built there to protect travellers.

The routes carried ideas as well as goods. Religions such as Buddhism and Islam spread along them, and technologies like papermaking reached Europe partly through these contacts. Unfortunately, diseases travelled too. The plague that killed millions of Europeans in the fourteenth century is believed to have moved west along the trade routes. The decline of the Silk Road began when sea routes became safer and cheaper. Ships could carry far larger loads than camels, so by the sixteenth century most long-distance trade had moved to the oceans.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the prices of goods rose along the routes because ----.
options: merchants had to pay to rest in caravanserais

camels could carry only very small loads
goods passed through the hands of many traders
diseases killed many of the merchants
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘goods passed through the hands of many traders’: 2. paragraf mallar bir tüccardan diğerine geçtikçe fiyatın her aşamada arttığını söylüyor. ‘rest’ ile fiyat arasında bağ kurulmuyor. ‘secret’ olan fiyat değil, ipeğin yapılış yöntemiydi. ‘camels’ gerilemenin nedeniyle ilgilidir. ‘killed’ veba Avrupalıları öldürdü, fiyatla ilgisi yok.

The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes which connected China with the Mediterranean world. It was used for more than fifteen hundred years, from about the second century BC until the fifteenth century. The name itself is quite modern: it was introduced by a German geographer in the nineteenth century, long after the routes had lost their importance.

Silk was the most famous product which moved west, and for centuries the Chinese kept the method of making it a secret. However, many other goods were also carried along the routes, including spices, paper, glass, horses and precious metals. Few merchants travelled the whole distance. Instead, goods passed from one trader to another, and prices rose at each stage. Cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara, where caravans stopped to rest and trade, grew rich as a result. Anatolia was also an important link, and many large inns called caravanserais were built there to protect travellers.

The routes carried ideas as well as goods. Religions such as Buddhism and Islam spread along them, and technologies like papermaking reached Europe partly through these contacts. Unfortunately, diseases travelled too. The plague that killed millions of Europeans in the fourteenth century is believed to have moved west along the trade routes. The decline of the Silk Road began when sea routes became safer and cheaper. Ships could carry far larger loads than camels, so by the sixteenth century most long-distance trade had moved to the oceans.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: why most of the water on Earth is salty

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how sea water is made drinkable and what problems this causes’: metin yöntemleri, sorunları ve çözümleri anlatıyor. ‘salty’ yalnızca giriş bilgisidir. ‘solar’ enerji çözümlerden biridir, ana konu değil. ‘rivers’ metinde yok. ‘first’ ilk tesisin tarihi anlatılmıyor.
exercises.passage:
Although water covers most of our planet, about 97 percent of it is salty and cannot be drunk. As populations grow and rainfall becomes less reliable, many dry countries are turning to desalination, the process of removing salt from sea water. Today there are more than fifteen thousand desalination plants around the world, and they provide drinking water for hundreds of millions of people.

Two main methods are used. The older one is based on heat: sea water is boiled, and the steam, which contains no salt, is collected and cooled until it becomes liquid again. The more common modern method is called reverse osmosis. In this process, sea water is pushed at very high pressure through a thin plastic sheet with tiny holes. Water molecules can pass through these holes, but the larger salt particles cannot.

Both methods have serious disadvantages. First, they need large amounts of energy, which makes the water expensive and, if the energy comes from fossil fuels, adds to carbon emissions. Second, every litre of fresh water leaves behind more than a litre of very salty waste called brine. When brine is poured back into the sea, it can harm fish and other creatures that live near the plant.

Engineers are working on solutions. New plants are increasingly powered by solar energy, and scientists are looking for useful ways to recover minerals from brine. Countries in the Middle East, which depend heavily on desalination, are expected to lead this research.

exercises.question: According to the passage, reverse osmosis works by ----.
options: pushing sea water through a sheet with tiny holes
boiling sea water and collecting the steam
adding minerals to the salty water
pouring brine back into the sea
cooling sea water until it freezes
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘pushing sea water through a sheet with tiny holes’: 2. paragraf suyun yüksek basınçla ince bir plastik tabakadan geçirildiğini söylüyor. ‘boiling’ eski, ısıya dayalı yöntemdir. ‘adding’ ters, mineraller tuzlu atıktan geri kazanılmaya çalışılıyor. ‘pouring’ atığın ne yapıldığıdır. ‘freezes’ metinde yok.

units.title: Bağlaçla yön değişimi
units.description: however ve in contrast ile yönü izle
units.guide:
## Strateji
Bağlaçlar metnin yön tabelalarıdır. *However, but, yet, still, in contrast, nevertheless* yön değişimi bildirir: sonra gelen cümle öncekinin tersini ya da bir sınırlamasını söyler. Yazarın asıl vurgusu çoğu zaman bu bağlaçtan **sonra** gelir. *Moreover, in addition* aynı yönde devam eder; *therefore, as a result, for this reason* sonuç bildirir.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Okurken bağlaçları işaretle.
2. Her bağlaçta sor: yön devam mı, dönüş mü, sonuç mu?
3. Dönüşten önceki kısmı "yaygın görüş ya da avantaj", sonrakini "yazarın vurgusu ya da sorun" olarak not et.
4. Ana fikir sorusunda dönüşten sonraki cümlelere öncelik ver.
5. Cümle tamamlamada boşluğun yanındaki bağlacın yönüne uymayan şıkları hemen ele.

## Örnek
*Plastic is cheap and strong. However, the same strength makes it a serious problem. Moreover, only a small part of it is recycled.*
- **However** → dönüş: olumlu özellik → sorun.
- **Moreover** → aynı yönde (sorun) devam.
- Ana fikir: plastik bir çevre sorunudur.

## Sınav ipucu
*Although, while, whereas* zıtlığı aynı cümle içinde kurar: "Although X, Y" yapısında Y, X'ten beklenmeyen bir sonuçtur. Boşluk *although* cümlesindeyse doğru şık mutlaka beklenene ters bir bilgi verir.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Most plastic is now recycled, so plastic waste is no longer a problem.
Some bacteria can break down plastic, but this is not yet a complete solution to plastic waste.
Plastic bottles break down quickly in rivers and oceans.
Japanese scientists invented a new type of plastic in 2016.
Enzymes from bacteria are used to make plastic from oil.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Some bacteria can break down plastic, but…’: metin keşfi anlatıyor, ardından “Still, scientists warn” ile sınırlarını veriyor. ‘recycled’ ters, plastiğin yalnızca küçük bir kısmı geri dönüştürülüyor. ‘quickly’ ters, yüzlerce yıl sürüyor. ‘invented’ yanlış, bilim insanları bakteri buldu. ‘Enzymes’ plastiği parçalar, petrolden plastik yapmaz.
exercises.passage:
Plastic is cheap, light and strong, which is why it is used almost everywhere. However, the same strength makes it a serious environmental problem. A plastic bottle may take hundreds of years to break down in nature, and only a small part of the plastic we use is recycled. The rest is burned, buried or ends up in rivers and oceans.

In 2016, a team of Japanese scientists made a surprising discovery. While they were studying samples from a recycling centre, they found a type of bacteria which could feed on PET, the plastic used in most drink bottles. The bacteria produce special proteins, called enzymes, that cut the long chains of the plastic into smaller pieces. These pieces can then be used as food by the bacteria.

At first, the process was extremely slow: it took the bacteria several weeks to break down a thin piece of plastic. Since then, however, researchers have improved the enzymes in the laboratory, and some modified versions now work many times faster. A French company has even built a factory where old plastic is broken down and turned into new bottles of the same quality.

Still, scientists warn that bacteria are not a magic solution. The method works on some types of plastic but not on others, and it is still more expensive than producing new plastic from oil. Moreover, it cannot remove the plastic which is already spread across the oceans. For this reason, most experts argue that using less plastic remains the most important step.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the bacteria found in 2016 ----.
options: could break down every type of plastic
worked faster than the modified versions
were first found in the ocean
were created by a French company
were discovered in samples from a recycling centre
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘were discovered in samples from a recycling centre’: 2. paragraf bunu açıkça söylüyor. ‘every’ yanlış, yöntem bazı plastik türlerinde işe yarıyor. ‘faster’ ters, değiştirilmiş türler daha hızlı. ‘ocean’ metinde bulunduğu yer değil. ‘French’ şirket fabrika kurdu, bakteriyi yaratmadı.

exercises.passage:
Earthquakes themselves rarely kill people; collapsing buildings do. This is why engineers say that the safety of a city depends largely on how its buildings are designed. Chile and Japan, for example, experience strong earthquakes, yet the number of deaths there is often lower than in countries where building rules are weak or ignored.

A building which is too stiff can break when the ground moves suddenly. Engineers therefore try to make structures that can bend slightly without collapsing. Steel frames and concrete that is strengthened with steel bars are commonly used for this purpose, because these materials can stretch a little before they fail. In contrast, walls made of heavy brick or stone without any support are among the most dangerous.

Some modern buildings go further. They are placed on special bearings, thick pads of rubber and steel, which separate the building from the ground. When an earthquake hits, the ground moves under these pads, but the building above moves much more slowly. Tall towers may also contain huge weights near the top that swing in the opposite direction and reduce the shaking.

Such technology is expensive, however, and most people do not live in new buildings. The real challenge is to strengthen the millions of older homes, schools and hospitals that were built before modern rules existed. Experts also point out that good rules are useless unless they are properly checked. After several recent disasters, investigations showed that many collapsed buildings had been built with poor materials.

nodes.description: Metin 1: Aşılar ve sürü bağışıklığı. Metin 2: Ekran süresi ve çocuklarda miyopi. ys5 kelimeleri: remove, spread, infection, virus, vaccine, vaccination, disease, respond ve 19 kelime daha.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Vaccines protect both individuals and whole communities through herd immunity.
Vaccines contain dangerous germs that often cause serious infections.
Measles has been removed from the world thanks to vaccines.
Herd immunity is only important for newborn babies.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Vaccines protect both individuals and whole communities…’: metin aşının hem bireyi hem toplumu nasıl koruduğunu anlatıyor. ‘dangerous’ ters, aşıdaki mikrop zayıf ya da ölüdür. ‘Measles’ yanlış; dünyadan silinen çiçek hastalığıdır. ‘newborn’ yalnızca bir örnektir. ‘everyone’ ters, bağışıklık yaygınsa hastalık yayılamaz.
exercises.passage:
Vaccines teach the body to fight a disease without the risks of catching it. A vaccine usually contains a weak or dead form of a virus or bacterium, or only a small part of it. When it is given, the immune system, which is the body's natural defence, learns to recognise the germ. If the person meets the real germ later, the body can respond quickly and stop the infection before it becomes serious.

Vaccines protect not only the people who receive them but also those around them. When most people in a community are immune, a disease cannot spread easily, because each sick person meets few others who can catch it. This effect is called herd immunity. It is especially important for people who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborn babies or patients with weak immune systems.

The level needed for herd immunity depends on how easily a disease spreads. Measles, which is one of the most infectious diseases known, requires about 95 percent of the population to be immune. For less infectious diseases, the level can be lower. If vaccination rates fall below this level, however, outbreaks can return quickly. This happened in several European countries in the 2010s, when measles cases rose after some parents refused to vaccinate their children.

Thanks to vaccines, smallpox was completely removed from the world in 1980, and polio has nearly disappeared. Yet health experts warn that these gains are not permanent. Herd immunity must be protected by every new generation.

options: Screens are the only cause of short-sightedness in children.

Reading books is better for children's eyes than using phones.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Myopia is increasing among children…’: metin artışı ve en güçlü kanıtın dışarıda geçen zamanla ilgili olduğunu anlatıyor. ‘only’ yanlış, “the picture is more complicated” deniyor. ‘lifestyle’ ters, hızlı değişim yalnızca genlerle açıklanamıyor. ‘better’ ters, kitap okumak da risk taşıyor. ‘expensive’ ters, tavsiye bedava.
exercises.passage:
Short-sightedness, or myopia, means that a person can see nearby objects clearly while distant ones look blurred. It usually begins in childhood and often gets worse until early adulthood. In recent decades, the condition has become far more common. In some cities of East Asia, around 80 percent of young people who finish school are now short-sighted, compared with much lower rates two generations ago.

Such a rapid change cannot be explained by genes alone, so researchers have looked at the way children live. Many people blame screens. Phones and tablets are held close to the eyes for hours, and studies have found a link between long screen time and myopia. However, the picture is more complicated. Children who read books for long periods are also at higher risk, which suggests that any close work may play a role.

The strongest evidence, in fact, concerns time spent outdoors. Several studies, including trials which were carried out in schools in China and Taiwan, have shown that children who spend more time outside are less likely to become short-sighted. Scientists believe that bright daylight releases a chemical in the eye which slows its growth. Indoor light is usually far weaker, even in a well-lit classroom.

For this reason, eye doctors now give parents simple advice. Children should take regular breaks from screens and books, and they should spend at least two hours a day outdoors. In contrast to many medical treatments, this advice costs nothing and has other benefits for health as well.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: House prices in big cities have fallen because wages rose quickly.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Housing in big cities has become very expensive…’: metin nedenleri, etkileri ve çözüm önerilerini sıralıyor. ‘fallen’ ters, fiyatlar ücretlerden hızlı arttı. ‘Investors’ nedenlerden yalnızca biri. ‘prefer’ yanlış, gençler buna zorlanıyor. ‘solved’ metinde böyle bir sonuç yok.
exercises.passage:
In many large cities around the world, housing has become very expensive. In places such as London, Sydney and Istanbul, house prices have risen much faster than wages over the past twenty years. As a result, an ordinary worker may need more than ten years of income to buy a small flat. Young people, who usually earn less than older workers, are hit the hardest.

There are several reasons for this situation. Cities attract people because they offer jobs, universities and services, so the demand for homes keeps growing. However, the supply of new homes has not kept up. Land in city centres is limited, and building is often slowed down by strict planning rules. Low interest rates, which made borrowing cheap for many years, also allowed buyers to pay higher prices. In addition, some homes are bought by investors and left empty or rented to tourists.

The effects go beyond personal finances. Many young adults are forced to live with their parents for longer, and some delay marriage or having children. Teachers, nurses and other key workers often cannot afford to live near the places where they are needed, so they face long journeys every day.

Governments have tried different solutions: some build social housing, which is rented at low prices to families on lower incomes, while others limit how much rents can rise each year. In contrast, many economists argue that the only lasting solution is to build more homes, especially near public transport.

exercises.passage:
In many large cities around the world, housing has become very expensive. In places such as London, Sydney and Istanbul, house prices have risen much faster than wages over the past twenty years. As a result, an ordinary worker may need more than ten years of income to buy a small flat. Young people, who usually earn less than older workers, are hit the hardest.

There are several reasons for this situation. Cities attract people because they offer jobs, universities and services, so the demand for homes keeps growing. However, the supply of new homes has not kept up. Land in city centres is limited, and building is often slowed down by strict planning rules. Low interest rates, which made borrowing cheap for many years, also allowed buyers to pay higher prices. In addition, some homes are bought by investors and left empty or rented to tourists.

The effects go beyond personal finances. Many young adults are forced to live with their parents for longer, and some delay marriage or having children. Teachers, nurses and other key workers often cannot afford to live near the places where they are needed, so they face long journeys every day.

Governments have tried different solutions: some build social housing, which is rented at low prices to families on lower incomes, while others limit how much rents can rise each year. In contrast, many economists argue that the only lasting solution is to build more homes, especially near public transport.
