exercises.passage:
Fast fashion is a business model in which clothes are designed, produced and sold very quickly at low prices. Some large companies bring new designs to their shops every week, and online sellers add thousands of items every day. As a result, people buy far more clothes than in the past. In many rich countries, the average person now buys about twice as many items as twenty years ago, but keeps each one for a much shorter time.

For shoppers, the model seems attractive: they can follow the latest trends without spending much money. However, the hidden costs are high, since making clothes requires huge amounts of water and energy. A single cotton shirt, for instance, may need over two thousand litres of water to produce. Many cheap clothes are made from polyester, a plastic material which releases tiny fibres into rivers and seas when it is washed.

The human costs are also serious, because most clothes are made in countries where wages are low and workers' rights are weak. In 2013, a factory building in Bangladesh collapsed and more than a thousand garment workers were killed. The disaster drew global attention to unsafe working conditions in the industry.

Some consumers are now changing their habits. Second-hand shops and clothing rental services have become popular, especially among young people who are concerned about the environment. Several governments are also discussing rules that would make companies responsible for the waste they create. Nevertheless, sales of fast fashion are still growing worldwide.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Göbekli Tepe has changed ideas…’: metin, tapınakların tarımdan sonra yapıldığı görüşünün bu alanla sorgulandığını anlatıyor. ‘villages’ ters, yapanlar avcı-toplayıcıydı. ‘Stonehenge’ ters, Göbekli Tepe binlerce yıl daha eski. ‘nobody’ ters, yeni araştırmalar insanların orada yaşadığını gösterdi. ‘human’ yanlış, taşlarda hayvan resimleri de var.
exercises.passage:
For a long time, archaeologists believed that people first built temples only after they had started farming and living in villages. Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site in south-eastern Türkiye, has challenged this idea. Its oldest parts were constructed about 11,500 years ago, which makes them thousands of years older than Stonehenge in England.

The site was first noticed in the 1960s, but its importance was not understood until a German archaeologist, Klaus Schmidt, began to dig there in 1995. He found large circles of stone pillars, some of which are more than five metres tall and weigh several tonnes. Many of the stones are decorated with pictures of wild animals such as foxes and birds. Some also have human arms and hands, which suggests that they may represent people or religious figures.

What surprised researchers most was the age of this discovery. At that time, the people of the region were hunter-gatherers, who lived by hunting animals and collecting plants. Moving and decorating such huge stones would have required hundreds of workers and careful planning. Schmidt therefore argued that the need to gather at the site may have encouraged people to settle down and later to grow crops. In other words, religion may have come before farming.

However, more recent research has shown that some people actually lived at the site, and the debate about its original purpose continues. The place was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018, and similar sites have since been found in the same region.

exercises.passage:
By 2050, about two thirds of the world's population is expected to live in cities. Feeding all these people will be a major challenge, especially as climate change makes traditional farming less reliable. One idea that has attracted attention is vertical farming, in which crops are grown indoors in tall stacks of shelves.

In a vertical farm, plants do not need soil or sunlight. Instead, their roots are placed in water that contains all the necessary nutrients, and the light comes from special LED lamps. Temperature, humidity and light are controlled by computers, so crops can be harvested all year round, regardless of the weather outside. Because no pesticides are needed, the vegetables are clean enough to be eaten without washing. Moreover, these farms use up to 95 percent less water than traditional fields, since the water is collected and used again.

Supporters also point out that vertical farms can be built inside cities, close to the people who buy their products. This reduces the distance that food has to travel and keeps vegetables fresh.

However, the method has important limitations. The lamps and climate systems use a large amount of electricity, which makes the food expensive and can increase carbon emissions. For this reason, vertical farms mainly grow leafy vegetables such as lettuce and herbs, which grow quickly and sell at high prices. Staple crops like wheat and rice, which feed most of the world, are still far too cheap to grow this way. Several well-funded companies have already closed because of high energy costs.

Because no pesticides are needed, the vegetables are clean enough to be eaten without washing. Moreover, these farms use up to 95 percent less water than traditional fields, since the water is collected and used again.

Supporters also point out that vertical farms can be built inside cities, close to the people who buy their products. This reduces the distance that food has to travel and keeps vegetables fresh.

For this reason, vertical farms mainly grow leafy vegetables such as lettuce and herbs, which grow quickly and sell at high prices. Staple crops like wheat and rice, which feed most of the world, are still far too cheap to grow this way. Several well-funded companies have already closed because of high energy costs.

units.title: Bilinmeyen kelimeyi tahmin et
units.guide:
## Strateji

Her bilinmeyen kelimede durup sözlüğe bakmak zaman kaybettirir ve anlamı böler. YDS’de sözlük yok, ama metin çoğu zaman ipucunu kendisi verir. Kelimenin türünü bul ve çevresine bak: **tanım** (virgülle açılan açıklama), **örnek** (*such as, for example*), **zıtlık** (*but, although, unlike*) ve **sonuç** (*so, because*).

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Kelimenin altını çiz ama okumayı bırakma; cümleyi bitir.

2. Türünü belirle: *-tion* isim, *-ly* zarf, *-ed* fiil ya da sıfat olabilir.

3. Virgülle açılan açıklamayı ara: *a planetarium, a building where…*

4. Zıtlık ya da sonuç bağlacına bak; anlamın yönünü (olumlu/olumsuz) verir.

5. Tahminini cümleye koy; anlam akıyorsa devam et.

## Örnek

*Near bright shores, the turtles become disoriented: they move towards the land instead of the sea.* İki noktadan sonraki açıklama kaplumbağaların yönünü şaşırdığını gösterir: *disoriented* ≈ yönünü kaybetmiş. Sözlüğe gerek kalmadı.

## Sınav ipucu

"closest in meaning" sorularında şıkkı metindeki kelimenin yerine koy ve cümleyi yeniden oku; anlam bozulmuyorsa doğru şıktır. Kelimenin en bilinen anlamına değil, o cümledeki anlamına bak.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
For most of human history, people could look up on a clear night and see thousands of stars. Today, however, more than a third of humanity cannot see the Milky Way, the band of light which crosses the night sky. The main reason is light pollution, the extra light that is produced by street lamps, buildings, cars and advertisements. This light does not stay on the ground. It spreads into the atmosphere, where it is scattered by tiny pieces of dust and gas, so the sky above a city shines like a weak lamp.

Scientists say that the problem is growing rapidly. One study, which used reports from thousands of volunteers around the world, found that the night sky became almost ten per cent brighter every year between 2011 and 2022. Pictures from space had shown a smaller increase, because many satellites cannot detect the blue light of modern lamps.

Light pollution is not only a problem for people who study the stars. Many creatures depend on darkness. Young sea turtles, for example, find the ocean by moving towards the brightest part of the sky, which is normally above the sea. Near bright shores, they are attracted to the land instead and often die. Insects are drawn to lamps, and birds which fly at night can lose their way. Even human sleep may be affected, since our bodies use darkness as a signal to rest.

The good news is that this kind of pollution is easy to reverse. When a light is switched off, the problem disappears immediately. Some towns now use lamps that point down to the ground, and several areas have been named dark sky places, where visitors can enjoy a sky full of stars.
options: why satellites are better than volunteers at measuring the brightness of the sky
the history of street lamps and modern advertisements in large cities
how artificial light hides the stars, harms living things and can be reduced
the way sea turtles use the stars to find their way to the ocean
the reasons why astronomers prefer to work in dark sky places
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how artificial light hides the stars, harms living things and can be reduced’: metin ışık kirliliğinin yıldızları gizlemesini, canlılara zararını ve çözümünü anlatır. ‘satellites’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, uydular artışı daha az göstermiştir; ‘history’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘turtles’ geçen şık yalnızca bir örnektir ve kaplumbağalar yıldızları değil gökyüzünün en parlak kısmını izler; ‘astronomers’ geçen şık metinde konu edilmez.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Every autumn, billions of birds leave their summer homes and fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places. Some small birds, which weigh less than a coin, cross deserts and oceans without a map, yet they often return to the same tree the following spring. How they manage this has been studied by scientists for more than a century, and the answer appears to be a combination of several senses.

First, many birds use the sun. During the day they can calculate direction from its position, and they adjust this information as the sun moves across the sky. Birds which travel at night use the stars instead. In a famous experiment, young birds were kept in a planetarium, a building where an artificial night sky is shown on the ceiling. When the pattern of stars was turned, the birds changed their direction too.

Second, birds seem to sense the magnetic field of the Earth, the invisible force which makes the needle of a compass point north. Researchers believe that special cells in the eye may detect this field, although the exact process is still being debated. Some birds also use their sense of smell, and others remember landscapes, rivers and coasts that they have seen on earlier journeys.

Because birds rely on several signals at once, a mistake in one sense can often be corrected by another. However, modern life creates new problems. Bright city lights confuse birds that travel at night, and tall glass buildings kill millions of birds every year. Understanding how birds find their way may therefore help us to protect them.
options: Most birds cannot find their way home without help from scientists.
Glass buildings are the main reason why birds lose their way.
Small birds travel shorter distances than large birds because they are weaker.
Birds use only their sense of smell when they cross oceans.
Birds find their way by combining several kinds of information, such as the sun, the stars and the magnetic field.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Birds find their way by combining several kinds of information…’: metin güneş, yıldızlar, manyetik alan, koku ve hafızanın birlikte kullanıldığını anlatır. ‘scientists’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘glass’ geçen şık son paragraftaki bir ayrıntıdır, ana fikir değildir; ‘weaker’ geçen şık desteklenmez; ‘smell’ geçen şık ‘only’ yüzünden yanlıştır.

Every autumn, billions of birds leave their summer homes and fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places. Some small birds, which weigh less than a coin, cross deserts and oceans without a map, yet they often return to the same tree the following spring. How they manage this has been studied by scientists for more than a century, and the answer appears to be a combination of several senses.

First, many birds use the sun. During the day they can calculate direction from its position, and they adjust this information as the sun moves across the sky. Birds which travel at night use the stars instead. In a famous experiment, young birds were kept in a planetarium, a building where an artificial night sky is shown on the ceiling. When the pattern of stars was turned, the birds changed their direction too.

Second, birds seem to sense the magnetic field of the Earth, the invisible force which makes the needle of a compass point north. Researchers believe that special cells in the eye may detect this field, although the exact process is still being debated. Some birds also use their sense of smell, and others remember landscapes, rivers and coasts that they have seen on earlier journeys.

Because birds rely on several signals at once, a mistake in one sense can often be corrected by another. However, modern life creates new problems. Bright city lights confuse birds that travel at night, and tall glass buildings kill millions of birds every year. Understanding how birds find their way may therefore help us to protect them.
options: discussed without agreement
fully proved
carefully hidden
quickly forgotten
widely accepted
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘discussed without agreement’. İpucu ‘although’: araştırmacılar bir şeye inanıyor ‘ama’ süreç hâlâ tartışılıyor, yani kesin değil. ‘fully proved’ ve ‘widely accepted’ bu zıtlıkla çelişir; ‘carefully hidden’ ve ‘quickly forgotten’ bağlama hiç uymaz.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Your body contains roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, and most of them live in your gut, the long tube that carries food from your stomach through the body. For a long time, these bacteria were seen mainly as a cause of infection. Today, however, scientists know that most of them are harmless, and many are actually helpful. Together they are called the gut microbiome, a community which includes hundreds of different species.

These tiny organisms do several important jobs. They break down parts of plant food, such as fibre, which our own bodies cannot digest. In the process they produce substances that feed the cells of the gut wall and help to keep it healthy. Some bacteria also make vitamins, and others train the immune system, the defence of the body against disease, to tell the difference between friends and enemies.

Researchers have found links between the microbiome and many conditions, including obesity, diabetes and even depression. In one well-known experiment, mice which received gut bacteria from fat mice gained more weight than mice which received bacteria from thin ones. However, most of these findings come from animals, and scientists warn that a link is not the same as a cause.

What can people do for their gut bacteria? The best advice is fairly simple. A varied diet that is rich in vegetables, fruit, beans and whole grains appears to support a richer community of species. Antibiotics, which kill harmful and helpful bacteria alike, should be used only when they are really needed.
options: Bacteria in the gut are the main cause of infections in humans.
Antibiotics are the best way to protect the gut microbiome.
Experiments on mice have proved that bacteria cause depression in humans.
Vitamins are produced only by the bacteria in our stomach.
The bacteria in our gut do many useful jobs and may affect our health in several ways.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The bacteria in our gut do many useful jobs…’: metin bağırsak bakterilerinin görevlerini ve sağlıkla bağlantılarını anlatır. ‘infections’ geçen şık eski görüştür, metin bunun yanlış olduğunu söyler; ‘antibiotics’ geçen şık tersini söyler, antibiyotik yararlı bakterileri de öldürür; ‘mice’ geçen şık yanlıştır, bağlantı neden değildir; ‘vitamins’ geçen şık ‘only’ yüzünden desteklenmez.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Heat waves, periods of unusually hot weather which last several days, are becoming more frequent and more intense as the climate changes. They are sometimes called a silent disaster, because their victims are rarely seen on television. Unlike floods or storms, heat does not destroy buildings, yet it can be one of the deadliest kinds of weather. In the summer of 2003, for example, tens of thousands of extra deaths were recorded in Europe.

The human body normally cools itself by sweating. When sweat dries on the skin, it removes heat. In very hot and wet air, however, sweat dries slowly, and the temperature of the body can rise to dangerous levels. The heart has to work harder to send blood to the skin, which puts extra pressure on people with heart or kidney problems. Heat stroke, the most serious result, can damage the brain and other organs if it is not treated quickly.

Some groups face greater risk than others. Elderly people often feel thirst less strongly, so they may not drink enough water. Babies, outdoor workers and people who live alone in small flats under the roofs of old buildings are also in danger. Cities make the problem worse, because concrete and stone store heat during the day and release it at night.

Fortunately, many heat deaths can be prevented. After 2003, France introduced a warning system in which elderly people who live alone are contacted by telephone during heat waves. Simple actions also help: drinking water regularly, staying in the shade and checking on neighbours.
options: describe how floods and storms destroy buildings in Europe
argue that elderly people should not live alone in cities
explain why heat waves are dangerous for health and how deaths can be prevented
compare the climate of France with that of other countries
show that television reports about heat waves are false
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain why heat waves are dangerous for health…’: metin sıcağın bedene etkisini, risk gruplarını ve önlemleri anlatır. ‘floods’ geçen şık yalnızca karşılaştırma için anılır; ‘argue’ geçen şık metinde savunulmaz; ‘compare’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘television’ geçen şık metindeki ‘rarely seen on television’ ifadesini çarpıtır.

nodes.title: Sosyal: platform ve müze
nodes.description: Metin 1: Platform ekonomisi (gig economy). Metin 2: Müzelerin dijitalleşmesi. ys5 kelimeleri: connect, vary, unite, union, labour, wage, pension, qualification ve 30 kelime daha.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
In the past, most workers had one employer, a fixed salary and a contract that gave them holidays and a pension. Today a growing number of people earn money in a different way. They deliver food, drive taxis or design websites through online platforms, which connect them with customers for a single task, or gig. This kind of work is known as the gig economy, and it has expanded rapidly since smartphones became common.

Supporters argue that gig work offers flexibility. Students, parents and people who already have another job can choose when and how much they work. For many, the platforms are also an easy way into the labour market, since few qualifications are required. Customers benefit too, because services are cheap and available at almost any hour.

Critics, however, point to the costs which are hidden behind this convenience. Most gig workers are treated as independent contractors rather than employees, so they usually receive no sick pay, no paid holidays and no pension. Their income can vary sharply from week to week, and they must pay for their own vehicles, fuel and phones. Moreover, their work is often controlled by an algorithm, a set of computer rules that decides who gets the next order and may punish a driver for refusing a job.

Governments have started to respond. In 2021 the highest court in the United Kingdom ruled that Uber drivers were workers, not self-employed people, and were therefore entitled to the minimum wage. The European Union has also adopted rules on platform work. The central question remains: how can flexibility be kept without leaving workers unprotected?
options: the advantages and disadvantages of earning money through online platforms
how to design a successful website for new customers
why students prefer fixed salaries to flexible work
the history of taxi services in the United Kingdom
how computer rules help drivers to earn more money
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the advantages and disadvantages of earning money through online platforms’: metin önce destekçilerin, sonra eleştirmenlerin görüşünü verir. ‘design’ geçen şık yalnızca bir iş örneğidir; ‘students’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘taxi’ geçen şık metinde bir tarih anlatısı yoktur; ‘computer’ geçen şık yanlıştır, algoritma sürücüyü cezalandırabilir.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Not long ago, the only way to see a famous painting was to travel to the museum where it hung. Today, millions of objects can be viewed on a phone. Large museums such as the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam have photographed hundreds of thousands of works and placed the images online, often free of charge. Visitors can zoom in until they see single marks of the brush, details that are hard to notice even when standing in front of the original.

The change accelerated in 2020, when most museums were closed during the pandemic. Institutions that had treated their websites as simple advertisements suddenly needed them to reach their audience. Virtual tours, online lectures and digital exhibitions were created in a few months, and some attracted more viewers than the buildings themselves had ever done.

Digital copies also help with preservation. Old manuscripts, which can be damaged by light and touch, can be studied by researchers through high-quality scans. When the National Museum of Brazil was largely destroyed by fire in 2018, much of its collection was lost forever, and the few digital records that existed became extremely valuable.

Yet not everyone is convinced that screens can replace a visit. Critics point out that a photograph cannot show the true size, surface or colour of a work, and that the experience of walking through quiet rooms is part of the meaning of art. Digital projects are also expensive to maintain, since files must be updated as technology changes. Most experts therefore see digital collections not as a replacement for museums, but as a door that invites new visitors inside.
options: Most museums closed permanently after the pandemic in 2020.
Putting museum collections online brings many benefits, but it cannot fully replace real visits.
Photographs show the size and colour of paintings better than the originals.
The National Museum of Brazil was destroyed because it had no digital records.
Digital projects are cheap and easy to keep up to date.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Putting museum collections online brings many benefits…’: metin yararları anlatır, son paragrafta sınırları verir. ‘permanently’ geçen şık yanlıştır, müzeler geçici kapandı; ‘photographs’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘Brazil’ geçen şıkta neden-sonuç uydurulmuştur; ‘cheap’ geçen şık ‘expensive to maintain’ ile çelişir.

nodes.title: Cümle çözümleme
nodes.description: Ünitenin metinlerinden uzun cümleler: ana fiili bul, which/they neyi gösteriyor, en uygun Türkçe karşılık

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘How they manage this has been studied by scientists for more than a century.’
options: manage
they
has been studied
scientists
more than
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘has been studied’. İskelet: özne ‘How they manage this’ (bir isim cümleciği: bunu nasıl başardıkları) + ana fiil ‘has been studied’ (edilgen) + ‘by scientists’. ‘manage’ öznenin içindeki yan cümlenin fiilidir; ‘they’ yan cümlenin öznesidir; ‘scientists’ eylemi yapandır, fiil değildir; ‘more than’ süre ifadesine aittir.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘they’ neyi göstermektedir? ‘Most gig workers are treated as independent contractors rather than employees, so they usually receive no sick pay.’
options: most gig workers
employees
customers
the platforms
governments
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘most gig workers’: ‘so’ ile başlayan ikinci cümlede ‘they’ ilk cümlenin öznesini sürdürür; hastalık parası alamayanlar işçilerdir. ‘employees’ karşılaştırma için anılır, işçiler çalışan sayılmaz; ‘customers’, ‘the platforms’ ve ‘governments’ bu cümlede yoktur.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘Antibiotics, which kill harmful and helpful bacteria alike, should be used only when they are really needed.’
options: harmful bacteria
helpful bacteria
the gut
people
antibiotics
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘antibiotics’: virgüllü ‘which’ yan cümlesi hemen önündeki öznenin ardından gelir. İskelet: ‘Antibiotics’ + ‘should be used’. ‘harmful bacteria’ ve ‘helpful bacteria’ yan cümlenin nesnesidir; ‘the gut’ ve ‘people’ cümlede geçmez.

options: Genç deniz kaplumbağaları okyanusu bulduktan sonra gökyüzünün en karanlık kısmına doğru ilerler.
Yaşlı deniz kaplumbağaları gökyüzünün en parlak kısmına doğru ilerleyerek okyanusu bulur.
Genç deniz kaplumbağaları gökyüzünün en parlak kısmına doğru ilerleyerek okyanusu bulur.
Genç deniz kaplumbağaları gökyüzünün en parlak kısmına doğru ilerleyince okyanusu bulamaz.
Genç deniz kaplumbağaları okyanusu bulmak için gökyüzünün en parlak kısmından uzaklaşır.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Researchers believe that special cells in the eye may detect this field.’

special
believe
cells
field

touch

options: Üstelik işleri nadiren bir algoritma, yani bir sonraki siparişi kimin alacağına karar veren bir dizi bilgisayar kuralı tarafından kontrol edilir.
Üstelik işleri bir algoritma kontrol eder ve sürücüler bir sonraki siparişi kendileri seçer.
Üstelik onlar çoğu zaman bir algoritmayı, yani bilgisayar kurallarını kontrol eder.
Üstelik işleri çoğu zaman bir algoritma, yani bir sonraki siparişi kimin alacağına karar veren bir dizi bilgisayar kuralı tarafından kontrol edilir.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
In 1929, while the Topkapı Palace in Istanbul was being turned into a museum, researchers found part of an old map painted on animal skin. It had been drawn in 1513 by Piri Reis, an Ottoman sea captain whose uncle, Kemal Reis, was also a famous sailor. The map shows the Atlantic Ocean, with the western coasts of Europe and Africa on one side and the eastern coast of South America on the other. Only about a third of the original map has survived.

What makes the map remarkable is not only its age. Piri Reis wrote notes on it explaining how it was made. He says that he combined about twenty older sources, including Arab and Portuguese charts, maps from the time of Alexander the Great and a map that had been drawn by Christopher Columbus. Since the map made by Columbus himself has never been found, the Piri Reis map is one of the few documents which may preserve his view of the lands he reached.

The map has also attracted many unusual theories. Some writers have claimed that the land at the bottom of the map is Antarctica, shown without ice, and that it must therefore have been drawn with help from an ancient lost civilisation or even from visitors from space. Historians reject these ideas. They explain that early mapmakers often bent coastlines to fit them on the page, and that the southern part of the map is more likely a distorted version of the South American coast.

Today the surviving piece is kept in the Topkapı Palace Museum, where it is rarely displayed because it is fragile.
options: the life of Kemal Reis and his journeys across the Atlantic
an old Ottoman map, the sources used to make it and the theories it has attracted
how Christopher Columbus drew the first map of South America
the reasons why Antarctica was free of ice in 1513
the history of the Topkapı Palace before it became a museum
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘an old Ottoman map, the sources used to make it and the theories it has attracted’. ‘Kemal’ geçen şık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır; ‘Columbus’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, onun haritası kayıptır; ‘Antarctica’ geçen şık tarihçilerin reddettiği bir teoridir; ‘Palace’ geçen şık yalnızca keşfin yeridir.

exercises.question: The author mainly aims to ----.
exercises.passage:
Meat grown in laboratories, sometimes called cultivated meat, is produced from animal cells rather than from animals that have been killed. The process begins when a small sample of cells is taken from a living animal. These cells are placed in large steel tanks, which are similar to the ones used to make beer, and are fed a liquid full of sugars, proteins and other nutrients. At the right temperature, the cells divide again and again until they form muscle and fat.

The first cultivated burger was presented in London in 2013. It had been produced by a Dutch scientist, Mark Post, and it reportedly cost more than 250,000 euros. Since then prices have fallen sharply, and in 2020 Singapore became the first country to allow the sale of cultivated chicken. The United States approved similar products in 2023.

Supporters believe that this technology could reduce some of the major problems of livestock farming. Raising animals uses huge areas of land and water, and cattle produce large amounts of methane, a powerful gas that warms the planet. Cultivated meat could also end the killing of billions of animals each year.

However, many questions remain. Producing cells on a large scale requires a lot of energy, and one study suggested that, if this energy comes from coal or gas, the benefit for the climate could be smaller than expected, or even negative. The products are still more expensive than ordinary meat, and some consumers do not trust food which is made in a factory. In 2023 Italy even passed a law that banned its production and sale. Whether cultivated meat becomes a normal part of our diet will depend on both cost and public opinion.
options: describe how cultivated meat is made and discuss its possible benefits and problems
persuade readers to stop eating ordinary meat at once
explain why Italy is the leader in cultivated meat
show that cultivated meat is already cheaper than ordinary meat
describe the life and work of the scientist Mark Post
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘describe how cultivated meat is made and discuss its possible benefits and problems’. ‘persuade’ geçen şık yanlıştır, yazar taraf tutmaz; ‘Italy’ geçen şık tersini söyler, İtalya üretimi yasakladı; ‘cheaper’ geçen şık ‘still more expensive’ ile çelişir; ‘Mark’ geçen şık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır.

exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards cultivated meat is best described as ----.
exercises.passage:
Meat grown in laboratories, sometimes called cultivated meat, is produced from animal cells rather than from animals that have been killed. The process begins when a small sample of cells is taken from a living animal. These cells are placed in large steel tanks, which are similar to the ones used to make beer, and are fed a liquid full of sugars, proteins and other nutrients. At the right temperature, the cells divide again and again until they form muscle and fat.

The first cultivated burger was presented in London in 2013. It had been produced by a Dutch scientist, Mark Post, and it reportedly cost more than 250,000 euros. Since then prices have fallen sharply, and in 2020 Singapore became the first country to allow the sale of cultivated chicken. The United States approved similar products in 2023.

Supporters believe that this technology could reduce some of the major problems of livestock farming. Raising animals uses huge areas of land and water, and cattle produce large amounts of methane, a powerful gas that warms the planet. Cultivated meat could also end the killing of billions of animals each year.

However, many questions remain. Producing cells on a large scale requires a lot of energy, and one study suggested that, if this energy comes from coal or gas, the benefit for the climate could be smaller than expected, or even negative. The products are still more expensive than ordinary meat, and some consumers do not trust food which is made in a factory. In 2023 Italy even passed a law that banned its production and sale. Whether cultivated meat becomes a normal part of our diet will depend on both cost and public opinion.
options: cautious and balanced
completely negative
openly enthusiastic
angry and critical
uninterested
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘cautious and balanced’: yazar yararları ve soruları birlikte verir, sonucu maliyet ve kamuoyuna bağlar. ‘completely negative’ ve ‘angry and critical’ olumlu noktaları yok sayar; ‘openly enthusiastic’ sorunları yok sayar; ‘uninterested’ ayrıntılı anlatımla uyuşmaz.

units.title: Zamanlı okuma
units.description: Metin başına 10 dakikada oku ve çöz
units.guide:
## Strateji

YDS’de 80 soruya 180 dakika var; okuma parçalarına metin başına yaklaşık **10 dakika** ayırabilirsin. Süreyi baştan bölmek panik yapmadan bitirmeni sağlar: her metne aynı planla girersen hangi aşamada ne kadar zamanın kaldığını hep bilirsin.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. **1 dk:** soru köklerine ve paragrafların ilk cümlelerine göz at.

2. **4 dk:** metni bir kez, geri dönmeden oku; her paragrafın konusunu bir iki kelimeyle not et.

3. **4 dk:** soruları çöz; ayrıntı sorusunda notundan ilgili paragrafa git.

4. **1 dk:** emin olmadığın soruyu işaretle ve devam et.

Bu ünitede her metni kronometreyle oku ve süreni yaz; hedefin her metinde 10 dakikanın altına inmek.

## Örnek

*Mexico introduced a tax on sugary drinks in 2014. Purchases of taxed drinks fell in the following years.* Notun: "Meksika vergisi → satış düştü". Soru Meksika’yı sorarsa metni baştan okumazsın, doğrudan bu paragrafa gidersin.

## Sınav ipucu

Tek bir soruya 2 dakikadan fazla takılma; işaretle ve geç. Ana fikir sorusunu en sona bırakmak çoğu zaman daha hızlıdır, çünkü o noktada metnin tamamını görmüş olursun.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
The ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland are more than just frozen water. They are also a record of the past climate of the Earth, which scientists can read like the pages of a book. Each year, snow falls on the surface and is slowly pressed into ice by the weight of the snow above it. As this happens, tiny bubbles of air are trapped inside, so each layer keeps a sample of the atmosphere from the year when it formed.

To study these layers, researchers drill long pieces of ice, called ice cores, which can be more than three kilometres long. The deepest cores from Antarctica contain ice that is around 800,000 years old. Back in the laboratory, the air in the bubbles is released and its carbon dioxide is measured. The ice itself also contains information. The chemical structure of the water shows how cold the air was when the snow fell, and layers of dust or ash point to dry periods or volcanic eruptions.

The results are striking. Over the last 800,000 years, the Earth has moved through several cycles of ice ages and warmer periods, and carbon dioxide has risen and fallen together with temperature. During this whole time, its level never went above about 300 parts per million. Today it is over 420, a level which has been reached mainly because of the burning of coal, oil and gas.

Unfortunately, this natural archive is disappearing. As mountain glaciers melt, their oldest layers are lost forever. For this reason, scientists have started to store ice cores from melting glaciers in a special cave in Antarctica, where they can be preserved for future generations.
options: Mountain glaciers are growing because of rising carbon dioxide.
Ice from glaciers and ice sheets keeps a long record of past climates that scientists can study.
Volcanic eruptions are the main cause of ice ages.
Ice cores are drilled mainly to find water for laboratories.
Snow in Antarctica falls only once every few hundred years.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Ice from glaciers and ice sheets keeps a long record of past climates…’: metin buzun bir iklim arşivi gibi okunmasını anlatır. ‘growing’ geçen şık tersini söyler, buzullar eriyor; ‘Volcanic’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, kül katmanları yalnızca patlamaları gösterir; ‘drilled’ geçen şıkta amaç yanlıştır; ‘once’ geçen şık ‘Each year, snow falls’ ile çelişir.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
On 25 December 2021, a rocket carrying the James Webb Space Telescope was launched from French Guiana. The telescope, which was developed by the space agencies of the United States, Europe and Canada, cost about ten billion dollars and took more than twenty years to build. It is the largest telescope that has ever been sent into space.

The main mirror of Webb is 6.5 metres wide, almost three times wider than that of the Hubble Space Telescope. Because it was too large to fit inside a rocket, it was made of eighteen smaller pieces which opened in space like the leaves of a flower. The telescope also differs from Hubble in the kind of light it collects. It observes mainly infrared light, a form of heat which the human eye cannot see. This is useful because light from the most distant galaxies has been stretched on its long journey through the growing universe, and it reaches us as infrared.

To detect such weak heat signals, the instruments must be extremely cold. Webb therefore has a huge sunshield, about the size of a tennis court, which protects it from the heat of the Sun, the Earth and the Moon. It works about 1.5 million kilometres from Earth, roughly four times further away than the Moon.

Since its first images were published in July 2022, Webb has produced a number of surprises. It has found galaxies that formed only a few hundred million years after the Big Bang, and it has detected water and carbon dioxide in the atmospheres of planets that travel around other stars.
options: the design of the Webb telescope and what it has discovered so far
the problems that delayed the launch of the Hubble telescope
how tennis courts are used to test space equipment
why the human eye can see infrared light
the history of rockets launched from French Guiana
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the design of the Webb telescope and what it has discovered so far’. ‘delayed’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘tennis’ geçen şık yalnızca bir boyut karşılaştırmasıdır; ‘human’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, göz kızılötesini göremez; ‘rockets’ geçen şık yalnızca fırlatma yeridir.

exercises.passage:
Sugary drinks such as cola and many fruit drinks are among the biggest sources of added sugar in the modern diet. A single can may contain around nine teaspoons of sugar, which is more than the World Health Organization recommends for a whole day. Because these drinks are linked to obesity, diabetes and damage to teeth, more than fifty countries have introduced special taxes on them.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Every day an adult breathes in about ten thousand litres of air. In many cities this air carries tiny particles which are produced by traffic, factories, power stations and the burning of wood and coal. The most dangerous of these are known as PM2.5, particles which are less than 2.5 thousandths of a millimetre wide, about thirty times thinner than a human hair.

Larger particles are usually stopped in the nose and throat, but PM2.5 can travel deep into the lungs. There they reach millions of tiny air bags where oxygen passes into the blood. The particles harm the lung tissue and cause swelling, which over many years can lead to breathing disorders and lung cancer. Some particles are so small that they even pass into the blood, and as a result they have been linked to heart attacks and strokes as well.

Children are particularly at risk, because their lungs are still developing and they breathe faster than adults. A long study in southern California found that children who grew up in more polluted areas had weaker lungs as young adults. Encouragingly, when the air in the same region became cleaner, the lungs of later groups of children developed better.

According to the World Health Organization, almost the entire population of the world breathes air that does not meet its guidelines, and air pollution is responsible for millions of early deaths each year. Experts say the most effective solutions are cleaner transport, cleaner energy and stricter limits for industry, although individuals can also reduce their exposure by avoiding busy roads on polluted days.
options: Larger particles are more dangerous than PM2.5.
Children breathe more slowly than adults and are therefore safe.
Tiny particles in polluted air can damage the lungs and other parts of the body.
Most of the population of the world breathes clean air.
Individuals cannot do anything to reduce their exposure.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Tiny particles in polluted air can damage the lungs and other parts of the body’. ‘Larger’ geçen şık tersini söyler, büyük parçacıklar burunda durur; ‘safe’ geçen şık yanlıştır, çocuklar daha hızlı nefes alır ve risk altındadır; ‘clean’ geçen şık DSÖ bilgisiyle çelişir; ‘anything’ geçen şık son cümleyle çelişir.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Imagine receiving a fixed sum of money from the government every month, whether you have a job or not, with no conditions attached. This is the idea of a universal basic income, which has been discussed by economists and philosophers for centuries. Supporters believe it could reduce poverty, give people security in a world of changing jobs and remove the complex rules of traditional welfare systems.

To test the idea, several experiments have been carried out. The most famous took place in Finland, where 2,000 unemployed people were paid 560 euros a month for two years, starting in 2017. Unlike ordinary benefits, the money was not reduced when they found work. The results were mixed. Participants were only slightly more likely to be employed than a comparison group, but they reported less stress, better health and greater trust in other people.

Another long-running project is managed by the charity GiveDirectly in rural Kenya, where thousands of villagers receive regular payments. Early findings suggest that people use the money to start small businesses, buy animals or improve their homes, rather than to stop working. An earlier experiment in a Canadian town in the 1970s similarly found that very few people stopped working, although young mothers and teenagers spent more time at home and in school.

The main objection is cost. Paying every adult enough to live on would require very high taxes, and critics fear that some people would choose not to work. Most experiments have also been small and temporary, so they cannot show what would happen if a whole country adopted the system permanently.
options: Basic income has been adopted permanently by Finland and Kenya.
Most people stop working when they receive free money.
Basic income is a new idea that was invented in 2017.
Traditional welfare systems are simpler than basic income.
Experiments with basic income have shown some positive results, but important questions remain.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Experiments with basic income have shown some positive results, but important questions remain’. ‘adopted’ geçen şık yanlıştır, deneyler geçicidir; ‘stop’ geçen şık bulgularla çelişir; ‘invented’ geçen şık ‘for centuries’ ile çelişir; ‘simpler’ geçen şık tersini söyler, geleneksel sistemlerin kuralları karmaşıktır.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1950, there were about six children under 15 for every person aged over 65 in the world. Today the gap is closing fast, and in many countries older people will soon outnumber children. This change, which is known as population ageing, has two main causes. People are living longer thanks to better medicine, food and clean water, and at the same time women are having fewer children.

Japan is often described as the most advanced example. Almost thirty per cent of its population is over 65, and in some rural villages schools have been closed because there are no longer enough pupils. Many European countries, as well as South Korea and China, are following the same path, and Türkiye, whose population is still relatively young, is also ageing more quickly than before.

The economic effects are serious. When the share of working-age people falls, fewer workers pay the taxes which fund pensions and health care for a growing number of retired people. Some governments have responded by raising the retirement age, while others encourage immigration or offer money to families who have more children. Robots and other technology are also being tested to support care for the elderly, particularly in Japan.

However, experts warn against seeing older people only as a burden. Many stay healthy and active for longer than previous generations, and they contribute a great deal as volunteers, consumers and grandparents who look after children. The challenge for societies is therefore not to stop ageing, which is a sign of success, but to adapt their workplaces, cities and welfare systems to it.
options: Japan is the only country whose population is ageing.
Older people are a burden that societies cannot afford.
Robots will soon replace all care workers in Japan.
Women in Türkiye are having more children than before.
Populations are getting older in many countries, which creates challenges but also reflects success.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Populations are getting older in many countries, which creates challenges but also reflects success’. ‘only’ geçen şık yanlıştır, birçok ülke aynı yoldadır; ‘afford’ geçen şık yazarın uyarısıyla çelişir; ‘Robots’ geçen şık abartılı bir ayrıntıdır, yalnızca deneniyorlar; ‘Women’ geçen şık tersini söyler, kadınlar daha az çocuk sahibi oluyor.

exercises.passage:
In 1950, there were about six children under 15 for every person aged over 65 in the world. Today the gap is closing fast, and in many countries older people will soon outnumber children. This change, which is known as population ageing, has two main causes. People are living longer thanks to better medicine, food and clean water, and at the same time women are having fewer children.

Japan is often described as the most advanced example. Almost thirty per cent of its population is over 65, and in some rural villages schools have been closed because there are no longer enough pupils. Many European countries, as well as South Korea and China, are following the same path, and Türkiye, whose population is still relatively young, is also ageing more quickly than before.

The economic effects are serious. When the share of working-age people falls, fewer workers pay the taxes which fund pensions and health care for a growing number of retired people. Some governments have responded by raising the retirement age, while others encourage immigration or offer money to families who have more children. Robots and other technology are also being tested to support care for the elderly, particularly in Japan.

However, experts warn against seeing older people only as a burden. Many stay healthy and active for longer than previous generations, and they contribute a great deal as volunteers, consumers and grandparents who look after children. The challenge for societies is therefore not to stop ageing, which is a sign of success, but to adapt their workplaces, cities and welfare systems to it.
options: great success
close friend
useful resource
new generation
heavy responsibility
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘heavy responsibility’: ‘However’ ile yazar bir görüşe karşı çıkar; ardından yaşlıların katkılarını sayar, demek ki ‘burden’ olumsuz bir kelimedir: taşınması zor yük. ‘great success’, ‘close friend’ ve ‘useful resource’ olumlu anlamlardır, uyarıyla uyuşmaz; ‘new generation’ yaşlılar için anlamsızdır.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Walking through the old parts of Istanbul, Cairo or Damascus, you may notice small, richly decorated buildings with large windows covered by metal bars. These are sebils, small public buildings which were common in Ottoman cities. Behind the bars, a man once sat and handed cups of water, or on special days sweet drinks, to anyone who passed by, free of charge.

Sebils were not built by the state. They were usually paid for by wealthy individuals, including members of the royal family, as an act of charity. In Islamic tradition, giving water to people who feel thirst is considered one of the most valuable good actions, so a sebil was a way for its founder to be remembered and rewarded. To make sure the service continued after the death of the founder, a foundation called a vakıf was established, whose income paid for the water and the staff.

Sebils were often attached to other buildings, such as mosques, schools or tombs, and placed at street corners where many people passed. A famous example is the Fountain of Ahmed III, which was built in 1728 in front of the main entrance of Topkapı Palace and has a small sebil at each of its corners. Its walls are covered with tiles and poems which praise the water and the ruler.

With the arrival of modern water pipes in the late nineteenth century, sebils gradually lost their purpose. Many were abandoned or destroyed, while others were converted into shops. Today some have been restored, and they remind visitors that access to clean water was once seen as a shared responsibility of the community.
options: Sebils were built by the state to sell water to travellers.
Sebils are modern shops found in Istanbul, Cairo and Damascus.
The Fountain of Ahmed III is the oldest building in Istanbul.
Sebils were charitable buildings that gave free water to the public in Ottoman cities.
Water pipes were invented to help sebils work better.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
In many European countries, when you buy a drink in a plastic bottle or a can, you pay a small extra amount, perhaps 25 cents. This money is not a tax. It is a deposit, and you get it back when you return the empty container to a shop. Such deposit-return schemes have existed for glass bottles for over a century, but in recent decades they have been expanded to plastic and metal containers as a way to fight litter and waste.

The idea works because it gives the empty bottle a value. People who might throw a bottle away keep it to collect the money, and if someone else drops one, collectors pick it up. In Germany, which introduced its scheme in 2003, more than 95 per cent of deposit bottles and cans are now returned. In countries without such systems, collection rates are often below 50 per cent.

High return rates bring other benefits as well. Containers that are collected separately are cleaner than those found in mixed household waste, so they can be recycled into new bottles rather than into lower-quality products. Most schemes use special machines, which scan the bottle, crush it and print a receipt that can be exchanged for cash in the shop.

There are, however, some disadvantages. Setting up the system is expensive, and shops have to provide space for machines and storage. Critics also argue that deposit schemes deal only with drink containers, while most plastic waste comes from other packaging. Nevertheless, the European Union now requires its members to collect 90 per cent of plastic bottles separately by 2029, and Türkiye has also begun to introduce a similar system.
options: how deposit-return schemes work and their advantages and disadvantages
the history of glass bottles in Germany
why plastic packaging should be banned completely
how shops in Europe set the prices of drinks
the reasons why recycling machines often fail
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how deposit-return schemes work and their advantages and disadvantages’. ‘history’ geçen şık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır; ‘banned’ geçen şık metinde savunulmaz; ‘prices’ geçen şık konu değildir; ‘fail’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.

İskelet: ‘which’ yan cümlesi Almanya’yı niteler; ana cümlede özne ‘more than 95 per cent of deposit bottles and cans’ + edilgen fiil ‘are returned’. ‘getirilmemektedir’ geçen şık olumsuzdur; ‘hedefleyen’ geçen şık anlamı hedefe çevirir; ‘kaldıran’ geçen şık ‘introduced’ ile çelişir; ‘dönüştürülmektedir’ geçen şık fiili ve nesneyi değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Sebils were usually paid for by wealthy individuals as an act of charity.’
options: Sebillerin parası genellikle devlet tarafından ödenirdi.
Varlıklı kişiler sebillerde genellikle para karşılığında su satardı.
Sebillerin parası genellikle bir hayır işi olarak varlıklı kişiler tarafından ödenirdi.
Sebillerin parası nadiren bir hayır işi olarak varlıklı kişiler tarafından ödenirdi.
Sebiller genellikle yoksul kişilere bir hayır işi olarak verilirdi.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Sebillerin parası genellikle bir hayır işi olarak varlıklı kişiler tarafından ödenirdi’. İskelet: özne ‘Sebils’ + edilgen ana fiil ‘were paid for’ + ‘by wealthy individuals’. ‘devlet’ geçen şık ödeyeni değiştirir; ‘satardı’ geçen şık anlamı bozar; ‘nadiren’ geçen şık ‘usually’ ile çelişir; ‘yoksul’ geçen şık fiili ve kişileri değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Hava kirliliği her yıl milyonlarca erken ölümden sorumludur.’
options: Air pollution is responsible for millions of early deaths every year.
Air pollution was responsible for a million deaths last year.
Millions of early deaths cause air pollution every year.
Air pollution is rarely responsible for early deaths.
Air pollution may be responsible for some deaths in the future.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Air pollution is responsible for millions of early deaths every year’. İskelet: özne ‘Air pollution’ + ‘is responsible for’ + ‘millions of early deaths’. ‘last’ geçen şık zamanı ve sayıyı değiştirir; ‘cause’ geçen şık neden-sonucu ters kurar; ‘rarely’ geçen şık anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘future’ geçen şık geniş zamanı geleceğe çevirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Bazı hükümetler emeklilik yaşını yükselterek karşılık vermiştir.’
options: Some governments have refused to raise the retirement age.
Some governments will respond by lowering the retirement age.
All governments responded by raising the age of workers.
Some governments have responded by raising the retirement age.
Some governments raised taxes in response to the retirement age.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Some governments have responded by raising the retirement age’. İskelet: özne ‘Some governments’ + ana fiil ‘have responded’; ‘-erek’ = ‘by + -ing’. ‘refused’ geçen şık anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘lowering’ geçen şık hem zamanı hem yönü değiştirir; ‘workers’ geçen şık ‘bazı’ yerine ‘all’ der ve nesneyi değiştirir; ‘taxes’ geçen şık yükseltilen şeyi değiştirir.

exercises.question: Although sugar taxes may reduce obesity, ----.
options: they were introduced in Mexico in 2014
critics say they hit poorer families hardest
drinks with more sugar are therefore cheaper
because people buy less sugar
which is recommended by doctors
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘critics say they hit poorer families hardest’: ‘Although’ olumlu bir noktanın ardından bir itiraz ister. ‘Mexico’ geçen şık zıtlık kurmayan bir ayrıntıdır; ‘therefore’ geçen şık anlamsız bir sonuçtur; ‘because’ geçen şık ana cümle değildir; ‘recommended’ geçen şık ‘which’ ile başladığı için ana cümle olamaz.

exercises.question: Webb has to be kept extremely cold ----.
options: but its sunshield keeps it warm
because it was launched in 2021
unless it is too large to fit inside a rocket
which the human eye cannot see
so that its instruments can detect weak heat signals
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘so that its instruments can detect weak heat signals’: soğukluğun amacı zayıf ısı sinyallerini algılamaktır. ‘sunshield’ geçen şık kalkanın işleviyle çelişir; ‘launched’ geçen şık ilgisiz bir neden verir; ‘rocket’ geçen şık anlamsız bir koşuldur; ‘human’ geçen şıkta ‘which’ niteleyecek bir isim bulamaz.

exercises.question: ----, older people will soon outnumber children in many countries.
options: Unless people live longer and healthier lives
As people live longer and families have fewer children
Although women are having fewer children
Because more children are born every year
Whose population is still young
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘As people live longer and families have fewer children’: iki neden yaşlıların sayıca üstün gelmesini açıklar. ‘Unless’ geçen şık nedeni koşula ve tersine çevirir; ‘Although’ geçen şık nedeni zıtlık gibi sunar; ‘born’ geçen şık sonuçla çelişir; ‘Whose’ ile başlayan şık niteleyecek bir isim olmadığı için dilbilgisel değildir.

nodes.title: Ünite ödülü
nodes.description: Üniteyi bitir, bonus XP kazan

nodes.title: Yarım deneme 1 (tanı)
nodes.description: YDS dağılımında 40 soru, 90 dakika. Gerçek sınavdan bir basamak kolay (B1–B1+); sonucuna göre zayıf soru tiplerini gör.

exercises.question: After the storm, council workers spent the whole morning trying to ---- the fallen trees from the main road.
options: attract
divide
remove
preserve
exceed
exercises.explanation: Fırtınadan sonra devrilen ağaçları yoldan kaldırmak gerekir; ‘remove ... from’ (bir yerden kaldırmak) kalıbı bunu verir. ‘attract’ (çekmek, ilgisini çekmek) ve ‘preserve’ (korumak) anlamca ters düşer; ‘divide’ (bölmek) ‘from the road’ ile anlam kurmaz; ‘exceed’ (aşmak) ise bir sınırı aşmak için kullanılır.

exercises.question: Prices in the city centre ---- greatly from one street to another, so it is worth comparing shops before you buy anything.
options: arise
vary
settle
consist
undergo
exercises.explanation: Fiyatlar sokaktan sokağa değişiyorsa karşılaştırmak mantıklıdır; ‘vary from ... to ...’ (... den ...e değişmek) tam bu anlamı verir. ‘consist’ her zaman ‘of’ ister; ‘undergo’ (geçirmek, maruz kalmak) nesne ister; ‘arise’ (ortaya çıkmak) ve ‘settle’ (yerleşmek, çözmek) fiyatlar için anlamsızdır.

exercises.question: The doctor said that her injury was not ---- and that she could go back to work within a few days.
options: voluntary
capable
formal
severe
equal
exercises.explanation: Birkaç gün içinde işe dönebiliyorsa sakatlık ciddi değildir: ‘severe’ (ağır, ciddi). ‘voluntary’ (gönüllü) ve ‘formal’ (resmî) bir sakatlığı nitelemez; ‘capable’ (yetenekli) insanlar için ve ‘of’ ile kullanılır; ‘equal’ (eşit) ise karşılaştırma gerektirir.

exercises.question: By the time we arrived at the station, the last train ----, so we had to take a taxi home.
options: has already left
already leaves
will already have left
is already leaving
had already left
exercises.explanation: ‘By the time + geçmiş zaman’ geçmişteki bir andan daha önce olan bir olayı anlatır, bu yüzden ‘had already left’ (past perfect) gerekir. ‘has already left’ şimdiye bağlanır; ‘already leaves’ ve ‘is already leaving’ şimdiki zamandır; ‘will already have left’ ise geleceği anlatır ve ‘arrived’ ile uyuşmaz.

exercises.question: If I ---- more free time, I would learn to play the guitar.
options: had
have
will have
would have
have had
exercises.explanation: Ana cümledeki ‘would learn’ ikinci tip (gerçek dışı şimdiki) koşul cümlesidir; if bölümü geçmiş zaman ister: ‘had’. ‘have’ ve ‘will have’ birinci tip koşula aittir; ‘would have’ if bölümünde kullanılmaz; ‘have had’ ise present perfecttir.

exercises.question: The new bridge ---- next year, and the journey to the city will become much shorter.
options: opened
has been opened
was opened
will be opened
had opened
exercises.explanation: ‘next year’ geleceği gösterir ve köprü açılan şeydir, yani edilgen gelecek zaman gerekir: ‘will be opened’. ‘opened’ ve ‘was opened’ geçmiş zamandır; ‘has been opened’ şimdiye kadar olanı anlatır; ‘had opened’ hem geçmiştir hem de etken yapıdır.

exercises.question: The woman ---- car was stolen last night has already called the police.
options: who
which
whom
where
whose
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘car’ kadına aittir; iyelik bildiren ilgi zamiri ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘who’ ve ‘whom’ kişinin kendisini, ‘which’ nesneleri niteler ve isimden önce iyelik anlamı vermez; ‘where’ ise yer bildirir.

exercises.question: You ---- wear a helmet when you ride a motorbike; it is the law in this country.
options: might
needn't
must
could
may
exercises.explanation: ‘it is the law’ zorunluluk bildirir, bu yüzden ‘must’ gerekir. ‘might’ ve ‘may’ olasılık, ‘could’ olasılık ya da yetenek anlatır; ‘needn't’ ise gerekli olmadığını söyler ve yasayla çelişir.

exercises.passage: The first Olympic Games (1)---- in 776 BC at Olympia, a religious site in the west of Greece. For several centuries, the Games consisted of only one event, a short running race (2)---- was about 190 metres long. Later, wrestling, boxing and horse racing were added to the programme. Travelling to Olympia was often dangerous because Greek cities were frequently at war with each other. (3)----, a special peace was announced before every Games so that athletes and visitors could travel safely. Winners did not receive gold medals; (4)----, they were given a simple crown made of olive leaves. The ancient Games came to an end in the fourth century AD, and it was not until 1896 that the modern Games were (5)---- in Athens.
exercises.question: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: took place
took part
broke out
ran out
came across
exercises.explanation: Oyunlar bir yerde ve tarihte düzenlenmiştir: ‘take place’ (gerçekleşmek, yapılmak). ‘took part’ katılmak demektir ve ‘in’ ister; ‘broke out’ savaş ya da yangın gibi kötü olaylar için kullanılır; ‘ran out’ (tükenmek) ve ‘came across’ (rastlamak) anlamca uymaz.

exercises.passage: The first Olympic Games (1)---- in 776 BC at Olympia, a religious site in the west of Greece. For several centuries, the Games consisted of only one event, a short running race (2)---- was about 190 metres long. Later, wrestling, boxing and horse racing were added to the programme. Travelling to Olympia was often dangerous because Greek cities were frequently at war with each other. (3)----, a special peace was announced before every Games so that athletes and visitors could travel safely. Winners did not receive gold medals; (4)----, they were given a simple crown made of olive leaves. The ancient Games came to an end in the fourth century AD, and it was not until 1896 that the modern Games were (5)---- in Athens.
exercises.question: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: who
where
whose
what
which
exercises.explanation: Boşluk ‘race’ (yarış) ismini niteleyen ve ‘was’ fiilinin öznesi olan bir ilgi zamiri ister: ‘which’. ‘who’ insanlar için kullanılır; ‘where’ yer bildirir ve özne olamaz; ‘whose’ ardından isim ister; ‘what’ ise bir ismi nitelemek için kullanılmaz.

exercises.passage: The first Olympic Games (1)---- in 776 BC at Olympia, a religious site in the west of Greece. For several centuries, the Games consisted of only one event, a short running race (2)---- was about 190 metres long. Later, wrestling, boxing and horse racing were added to the programme. Travelling to Olympia was often dangerous because Greek cities were frequently at war with each other. (3)----, a special peace was announced before every Games so that athletes and visitors could travel safely. Winners did not receive gold medals; (4)----, they were given a simple crown made of olive leaves. The ancient Games came to an end in the fourth century AD, and it was not until 1896 that the modern Games were (5)---- in Athens.
exercises.question: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: For this reason
On the contrary
For instance
Similarly
In short
exercises.explanation: Önceki cümle yolculuğun tehlikeli olduğunu söyler; özel bir barış ilan edilmesi bunun sonucudur, bu yüzden ‘For this reason’ gerekir. ‘On the contrary’ önceki fikri reddeder; ‘For instance’ örnek verir; ‘Similarly’ benzer bir durum ekler; ‘In short’ ise özet yapar, oysa barış ilanı yeni bir bilgidir.

exercises.passage: The first Olympic Games (1)---- in 776 BC at Olympia, a religious site in the west of Greece. For several centuries, the Games consisted of only one event, a short running race (2)---- was about 190 metres long. Later, wrestling, boxing and horse racing were added to the programme. Travelling to Olympia was often dangerous because Greek cities were frequently at war with each other. (3)----, a special peace was announced before every Games so that athletes and visitors could travel safely. Winners did not receive gold medals; (4)----, they were given a simple crown made of olive leaves. The ancient Games came to an end in the fourth century AD, and it was not until 1896 that the modern Games were (5)---- in Athens.
exercises.question: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: therefore
instead
similarly
besides
meanwhile
exercises.explanation: Kazananlar altın madalya yerine zeytin dalından bir taç alıyordu: ‘instead’ (onun yerine). ‘therefore’ sonuç bildirir; ‘similarly’ benzerlik kurar; ‘besides’ ekleme yapar; ‘meanwhile’ ise aynı anda olan başka bir olayı anlatır.

exercises.passage: The first Olympic Games (1)---- in 776 BC at Olympia, a religious site in the west of Greece. For several centuries, the Games consisted of only one event, a short running race (2)---- was about 190 metres long. Later, wrestling, boxing and horse racing were added to the programme. Travelling to Olympia was often dangerous because Greek cities were frequently at war with each other. (3)----, a special peace was announced before every Games so that athletes and visitors could travel safely. Winners did not receive gold medals; (4)----, they were given a simple crown made of olive leaves. The ancient Games came to an end in the fourth century AD, and it was not until 1896 that the modern Games were (5)---- in Athens.
exercises.question: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: occupied
divided
reduced
exposed
launched
exercises.explanation: Modern oyunlar 1896’da Atina’da başlatılmıştır: ‘launched’ (başlatılmak). ‘occupied’ (işgal edilmek) ve ‘exposed’ (maruz bırakılmak) oyunlar için anlamsızdır; ‘divided’ (bölünmek) ve ‘reduced’ (azaltılmak) da paragraftaki ‘sona erdi ... ancak 1896’da’ akışına uymaz.

exercises.question: Although the hotel was very expensive, ----.
options: the rooms were small and the service was poor
because it was close to the beach
unless you book your room early
so we stayed there for two weeks
which was why many tourists chose it
exercises.explanation: ‘Although’ zıtlık ister: otel pahalı olmasına rağmen odalar küçük ve hizmet kötüydü (‘the rooms were small and the service was poor’). ‘because’ ve ‘unless’ ile başlayan yan cümleler ana cümle olamaz; ‘so’ ile başlayan seçenek ‘although’ ile birlikte kullanılmaz; ‘which was why’ ise pahalılığı turistlerin seçme nedeni yapar ve zıtlık kurmaz.

exercises.question: ----, she decided to take a taxi to the airport.
options: Unless she missed the bus
Whereas her flight was cancelled
Since she was carrying three heavy suitcases
So that she could enjoy the walk
As soon as she will arrive
exercises.explanation: Taksiye binmenin nedeni ağır bavullardır: ‘Since she was carrying three heavy suitcases’. ‘Unless’ koşulu geçmişteki karara uymaz; ‘Whereas’ karşılaştırma bildirir ve uçuş iptal olduysa havaalanına gitmek anlamsızdır; ‘walk’ içeren seçenek taksiyle çelişir; ‘As soon as’ ile ‘will’ birlikte kullanılmaz.

exercises.question: If the government had invested more money in public transport, ----.
options: fewer people would have needed a car
fewer people will need a car
traffic is getting worse every year
more buses were bought last year
the roads had been much safer
exercises.explanation: Üçüncü tip koşul cümlesi (‘had invested’) ana cümlede ‘would have + V3’ ister: ‘fewer people would have needed a car’. ‘will need’ birinci tip koşula aittir; ‘getting worse’ ve ‘bought’ içeren seçeneklerde ‘would’ yoktur ve koşulla bağ kurmaz; ‘had been’ ise ana cümlede kullanılamaz.

exercises.question: The new phone has become so popular ----.
options: because its price is very high
that many shops cannot keep enough of it in stock
although few people had heard of it
which was produced in Korea
as it was hardly advertised
exercises.explanation: ‘so + sıfat’ yapısı ‘that’ ile sonucu bildirir: telefon o kadar popüler oldu ki dükkânlar yeterince stok tutamıyor (‘that many shops cannot keep enough of it in stock’). ‘because’, ‘although’, ‘which’ ve ‘as’ ile başlayan seçenekler ‘so ... that’ kalıbını tamamlamaz; ayrıca ‘price’ ve ‘advertised’ içeren nedenler popülerliği açıklamaz.

exercises.question: ----, scientists still do not fully understand how the human brain stores memories.
options: Thanks to modern brain scanners
Because they have done so much research
Now that the problem has been solved
Despite decades of careful research
So that people can remember more
exercises.explanation: ‘still do not fully understand’ beklentinin tersini anlatır, bu yüzden zıtlık bildiren ‘Despite decades of careful research’ gerekir. ‘Thanks to’ ve ‘Because’ ile başlayan seçenekler anlamayı açıklayan bir neden verir ve cümleyle çelişir; ‘solved’ içeren seçenek sorunun çözüldüğünü söyler; ‘So that’ amaç bildirir ve anlamsızdır.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Most of the people who took part in the survey said that they read fewer books than they did ten years ago.
options: Ankete katılan insanların hepsi, on yıl öncesine göre daha fazla kitap okuduklarını söyledi.
Ankete katılan insanların çoğu, on yıl önce de az kitap okuduklarını söyledi.
Anketi hazırlayan insanların çoğu, son on yılda hiç kitap okumadıklarını söyledi.
Ankete katılan insanların bazıları, on yıl sonra daha az kitap okuyacaklarını söyledi.
Ankete katılan insanların çoğu, on yıl öncesine göre daha az kitap okuduklarını söyledi.
exercises.explanation: ‘Most of the people who took part in the survey’ (ankete katılan insanların çoğu) ve ‘fewer books than they did ten years ago’ (on yıl öncesine göre daha az kitap) öğelerinin hepsi ‘Ankete katılan insanların çoğu, on yıl öncesine göre daha az kitap okuduklarını söyledi.’ cümlesinde vardır. ‘hepsi ... fazla’ hem miktarı hem karşılaştırmayı bozar; ‘hazırlayan’ katılanları hazırlayanlara çevirir; ‘okuyacaklarını’ zamanı geleceğe taşır; ‘önce de az’ ise karşılaştırmayı kaldırır.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Yeni yasa, şehir merkezinde araba kullanmayı yasaklamadı ama park ücretlerini iki katına çıkardı.
options: The new law banned driving in the city centre and also doubled parking fees.
The new law did not ban driving in the city centre, but it reduced parking fees by half.
Although the new law will ban driving in the city centre, parking fees will remain the same.
The new law did not ban driving in the city centre, but it doubled parking fees.
The new law did not double parking fees, but it banned driving outside the city centre.
exercises.explanation: ‘yasaklamadı’ (did not ban) ve ‘iki katına çıkardı’ (doubled) öğeleri ‘The new law did not ban driving in the city centre, but it doubled parking fees.’ cümlesinde doğru verilir. ‘also’ içeren cümle yasağı varmış gibi gösterir; ‘half’ ücretleri yarıya indirir; ‘remain’ içeren cümle gelecek zamanı ve ücretlerin değişmediğini anlatır; ‘outside’ ise anlamı tamamen tersine çevirir.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Unless the bridge is repaired soon, the villagers will have to travel an extra twenty kilometres to reach the hospital.
options: Köprü yakında onarılırsa köylüler hastaneye ulaşmak için fazladan yirmi kilometre yol gitmek zorunda kalacak.
Köprü onarılmadığı için köylüler hastaneye ulaşmak için fazladan yirmi kilometre yol gitmek zorunda kaldı.
Köprü yakında onarılmazsa köylüler hastaneye ulaşmak için fazladan yirmi kilometre yol gitmek zorunda kalacak.
Köprü yakında onarılmazsa köylüler hastaneye yirmi kilometreden daha kısa bir yoldan ulaşabilecek.
Köylüler hastaneye gitmek için yirmi kilometre yürüdükleri sürece köprü onarılmayacak.
exercises.explanation: ‘Unless’ (-mezse) ve ‘will have to’ (zorunda kalacak) öğeleri ‘Köprü yakında onarılmazsa köylüler ... fazladan yirmi kilometre yol gitmek zorunda kalacak.’ cümlesinde doğru karşılanır. ‘onarılırsa’ koşulu tersine çevirir; ‘onarılmadığı için ... kaldı’ koşulu nedene, zamanı geçmişe çevirir; ‘kısa’ içeren cümle fazladan yolu kısaltır; ‘yürüdükleri sürece’ ise öznesi ve anlamı farklı bir cümledir.

exercises.passage: Microplastics are tiny pieces of plastic, smaller than five millimetres, which are produced when larger plastic objects slowly break down. In recent years, they have been found almost everywhere: in the ocean, in soil, in the air and even in the water that comes out of our taps. A study published in 2018 tested bottled water from several countries and found plastic particles in more than ninety percent of the samples. The study also showed that bottled water often contained more particles than tap water, possibly because small pieces are released from the bottle and its cap. Scientists are still not sure how harmful these particles are for human health. Most of the plastic we swallow is thought to pass through the body without being absorbed. However, the smallest particles might enter the blood, and some researchers worry that the chemicals they carry could cause problems over a long period. At the moment, there is not enough reliable evidence to say whether the amounts found in drinking water are dangerous, and the World Health Organization has called for more research rather than immediate action. In the meantime, experts suggest some simple steps. Filters used in many homes can remove a large proportion of the particles, and drinking tap water instead of bottled water seems to reduce exposure. In the long run, however, the only real solution is to produce and throw away less plastic, since the problem begins long before the water reaches our glass.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: what is known and not yet known about plastic particles in the water we drink
why bottled water is healthier than tap water
how plastic bottles are produced in different countries
the history of the World Health Organization
the dangers of the chemicals used in home water filters
exercises.explanation: Metin içme suyundaki mikroplastikler hakkında bilinenleri (2018 çalışması) ve henüz bilinmeyenleri (sağlığa etkisi) anlatır: ‘what is known and not yet known about plastic particles in the water we drink’. ‘healthier’ içeren seçenek metne ters düşer, çünkü şişe suyunda daha çok parçacık bulunmuştur; şişelerin üretimi (‘produced’) ve örgütün tarihi (‘history’) metinde anlatılmaz; filtreler (‘filters’) tehlikeli değil, çözüm olarak sunulur.

At the moment, there is not enough reliable evidence to say whether the amounts found in drinking water are dangerous, and the World Health Organization has called for more research rather than immediate action. In the meantime, experts suggest some simple steps. Filters used in many homes can remove a large proportion of the particles, and drinking tap water instead of bottled water seems to reduce exposure. In the long run, however, the only real solution is to produce and throw away less plastic, since the problem begins long before the water reaches our glass.
exercises.question: According to the passage, the study published in 2018 found that ----.
options: plastic particles were present in fewer than half of the samples
tap water was completely free of plastic particles
bottled water often contained more plastic particles than tap water
most of the plastic people swallow enters the blood
bottle caps stop plastic from getting into the water
exercises.explanation: Metinde çalışmanın şişe suyunda musluk suyundan daha çok parçacık bulduğu söylenir: ‘bottled water often contained more plastic particles than tap water’. Parçacıklar örneklerin yüzde doksanından fazlasında bulunmuştur, yarıdan azında (‘fewer than half’) değil; musluk suyunun tamamen temiz olduğu (‘completely free’) söylenmez; yutulan plastiğin çoğunun kana karıştığı (‘enters the blood’) değil, vücuttan geçtiği belirtilir; kapakların (‘caps’) ise parçacık bıraktığı düşünülür.

exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that the World Health Organization ----.
options: has banned the sale of bottled water in several countries
does not think there is enough evidence yet to take urgent measures
carried out the 2018 study on bottled water
believes that microplastics are completely harmless
advises people to drink bottled water instead of tap water

therefore
instead

exercises.passage: For centuries, learning to write by hand was one of the first things children did at school. Today, however, many young people spend far more time typing on keyboards and phones than holding a pen. In some countries, schools have reduced the hours given to handwriting lessons, and a few have stopped teaching joined-up writing altogether. Supporters of this change argue that typing is faster and is the skill that students will actually need in their future jobs. Not everyone agrees. A number of studies suggest that writing by hand helps the brain in ways that typing does not. In one experiment, university students who took notes with a pen remembered the main ideas of a lecture better than those who used a laptop. The researchers, who repeated the test several times, believe that because writing by hand is slower, students cannot copy every word. Instead, they have to think about the information and decide what is important, which helps them understand it more deeply. Handwriting may also be important for young children who are learning to read. When children form letters with their own hands, they seem to recognise them more quickly than when they simply press a key. None of this means that schools should go back to the past. Most experts believe that children need both skills. Keyboards are clearly here to stay, but it would be a mistake to throw away the pen too quickly.
exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Schools should stop teaching typing and return to traditional handwriting lessons.
University students prefer laptops because they can take notes faster.
Handwriting lessons are the main reason why some children learn to read late.
Joined-up writing has been banned in most countries around the world.
Although typing is now more common, writing by hand still seems to offer important benefits for learning.
exercises.explanation: Metin, klavye yaygınlaşsa da elle yazmanın öğrenmeye katkılarını anlatır: ‘Although typing is now more common, writing by hand still seems to offer important benefits for learning.’ Yazar okulların geçmişe dönmesi gerekmediğini söyler, yani ‘return’ içeren seçenek metne terstir; dizüstü bilgisayar tercihi (‘laptops’) yalnızca bir deneyin ayrıntısıdır; okumayı geciktirme (‘late’) ve yasaklama (‘banned’) metinde yoktur.
